* **Abiy, sworn in for a new term, insists Ethiopia must have Red Sea access:** Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed [told](https://substack.com/redirect/898c4203-b1d8-4133-8e81-47f4d70ca33d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Parliament Monday, as he was sworn in for another five-year term, that Ethiopia will work to secure a Red Sea port, saying "based on the principle of give and take, we will work diligently to ensure that Ethiopia has an outlet to the sea" and calling access critical to the country's "civilization."
* His remarks came a day after Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan, and Somalia met in New Alamein and declared that governance of the Red Sea is the "exclusive responsibility" of the region's coastal states. Eritrea has accused Ethiopia of seeking to reassert control over its coast, which it lost when Eritrea gained its independence from Ethiopia in 1993.
* **ISIS attack kills Iraqi federal policeman near Kirkuk, first since U.S. withdrawal:** At least one Iraqi federal policeman was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/bc481021-b68e-4a14-88f8-22ced516663e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and four wounded Monday when Islamic State militants attacked a federal police regiment near Hawija, about 70 km southwest of Kirkuk, using semi-automatic machine guns and sniper fire, two security sources told Reuters. No group has claimed responsibility, but security and army sources said ISIS militants, who retain sleeper cells in the area, were involved.
* It is the first reported ISIS assault on Iraqi security forces since the U.S. completed its military withdrawal from Iraq on Sept. 30.
* **Russian bombs kill seven, injure over 60 in Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia:** Three Russian bombs [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/23eaafe1-1b18-4fa5-a087-6656edca6a5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) different areas of the northeastern Ukrainian city Kharkiv on Monday, killing six people and injuring 59, according to regional governor Oleh Syniehubov. Three of those injured in Monday's attacks on Kharkiv were children.
* Elsewhere on Monday, a Russian drone hit an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, injuring three people who were trapped on the ninth floor, according to that region's governor.
* Russian airstrikes also killed one person in Sloviansk in the Donetsk region.
* **Russia says Ukrainian drones struck Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, killing one:** Ukrainian drones [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/c63af739-ec21-4da5-9950-71d252e535a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a laboratory building and a radioactive waste processing facility at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant overnight on Monday, killing a driver delivering food to plant workers, according to Alexei Likhachev, head of Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom, who said there was no threat to nuclear safety.
* **Ukraine blames Russian drones for sinking of grain ship in Romanian waters; two dead:** Romania's Interior Ministry [said](https://substack.com/redirect/23eaafe1-1b18-4fa5-a087-6656edca6a5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two people were killed and 11 rescued after a grain ship caught fire and sank Monday in Romania's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea; the ministry did not identify the cause of the fire. Azerbaijani and Indian nationals were reportedly aboard.
* Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for the fire, condemning in a Monday post on X the "horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkiye."
* **Kuwait revokes citizenship of 415 more people, including billionaire Mahmoud Haider:** Kuwait [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/de90d6ff-f175-4f01-af1f-15353513a797?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) six decrees published in its official gazette stripping 415 people of citizenship, including billionaire businessman Mahmoud Haider, along with dependents who obtained nationality through those whose citizenship was revoked.
* The Gulf state announced a citizenship review campaign in 2024, targeting fraudulent claims, including those involving individuals reporting dual nationality or those who acquired it through marriage. It has expanded this year to politicians, footballers, and musicians, including 1982 World Cup goalkeeper Ahmed al-Tarabulsi and singer Abdulmohsen Al Muhanna. Rights groups estimate at least 50,000 people have lost citizenship since 2024.
* **Former German intelligence chief arrested on suspicion of buying classified documents for foreign spy agency:** Former Federal Intelligence Service chief August Hanning was [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/2aff1d88-8e6e-4f58-a938-c1407ace614b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday on suspicion of paying a former office manager at the agency for roughly 2,000 documents, including classified material and senior intelligence briefings prepared for the chancellery, and using them to draft an analysis for an officer of an unnamed foreign intelligence service, according to German federal prosecutors.
* Prosecutors allege the arrangement began in 2010, five years after Hanning left the agency, and that he also shared political information with a representative of a second foreign intelligence service. The office manager, identified only as Manfred D., was also arrested.
* The case does not involve Russia, according to the German newspaper Suddeutsche Zeitung.
* **Police clash with Kosovo protesters over bid to curb Hague war crimes court:** Police [used](https://substack.com/redirect/7030ab0f-9da2-4625-986d-463e5f66f150?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tear gas and water cannons Monday evening against several hundred protesters, including veterans and supporters of the ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army, outside Parliament in Pristina after lawmakers adjourned without passing amendments limiting the powers of the controversial Kosovo Specialist Chambers court. Twelve people were injured, including 11 civilians, according to a Pristina hospital emergency director.
* The amendments, which passed a first reading earlier Monday, would cap the court's sentences at 15 years, allow these to be served in Kosovo and permit appeals to Kosovo's Supreme Court. They were forwarded by the opposition Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK) and halted by Prime Minister Albin Kurti's governing Vetevendosje party.
* The court remains controversial in Kosovo, where the KLA, which the court was created to prosecute, is held in high esteem by many in the country's Albanian population after its fight against the Serbian-dominated Yugoslav government during Kosovo's 1998-1999 war.
* **Hundreds flee RSF assaults in Sudan 's Blue Nile region: **Hundreds of residents have [fled](https://substack.com/redirect/99c083e3-3703-43f3-9f49-ab53fbdf500f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the localities of Jabal Al-Nimr and Minza in Sudan's southeastern Blue Nile region after recent Rapid Support Forces attacks, the region's Humanitarian Aid Commission said on Monday. Most are heading toward the town of Al-Azaza and a settlement known as Village 6, raising concerns over civilian protection and shortages of essential supplies.
* **Cuba says it has "channels of communication" with the U.S. but no negotiations, and is preparing to defend itself: **Cuba's charge d'affaires in Washington, Lianys Torres Rivera, [told](https://substack.com/redirect/3b6603b9-f20f-40e1-ab2a-10931fbefa9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Reuters on Monday that Havana and Washington maintain "channels of communication"--including meetings, phone calls, and WhatsApp messages--but are not in formal negotiations and have made no progress toward restarting official talks.
* Rivera's remarks contradict President Donald Trump's claim last month at the UN that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was "deep into negotiations" with Havana.
* Torres Rivera said Cuba remains open to "respectful" dialogue with the U.S. but is "not naive" about Trump's threats and is expanding its defense preparations, saying "we are increasing our capabilities now more than ever before."
* She also noted that Cuba's "red line" remains changes to its political system.
* **Mexico asks U.S. for evidence of alleged cross-border gunfire at Coast Guard personnel:** Mexican**** President Claudia Sheinbaum [said](https://substack.com/redirect/b75dacfc-913e-4143-9b5d-e36e61cc1634?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday her government has requested evidence from U.S. authorities about allegations that shots were fired from the Mexican side of the border at U.S. personnel, saying "we asked for all the evidence because we have no evidence" and that no National Guard, Army, or Navy personnel detected shots fired from Mexican territory toward the U.S.
* The comments came a day after U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson said on X that "shots were fired at U.S. Coast Guard personnel" in an area where Tamaulipas meets Texas.
* The incident follows Mexico's announcement of "Operation Mirror" on Sunday evening, a joint border security effort deploying 500 troops, helicopters, drones and anti-drone equipment along the frontier. Despite deepening security collaboration, Sheinbaum has repeatedly denied that her government would allow a U.S. military intervention on Mexican soil.
* **Parti Qu ebecois wins Quebec election, complicating Carney's unity push against Trump: **The separatist party Parti Quebecois, [led](https://substack.com/redirect/ad985d20-8d1c-4321-a787-541d04f37a04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, won Quebec's election Monday, according to early projections from public broadcaster Radio-Canada, though it remains too early to say whether the party secured a majority in the province's legislature.
* The result, widely expected before the vote, will jettison the center-right Coalition Avenir Quebec government, which has been in office since 2018.
* St-Pierre Plamondon has promised a referendum on leaving Canada, but only once Trump is out of the White House. Previous independence referendums failed in 1980 and 1995, and current polling puts support for a separation at around 30 percent.
* St-Pierre Plamondon pledged to work with Carney when it suits the province's interests; his party notably diverges from Ottawa in its calls to reduce immigration, cut Quebec's ties to the British monarchy, and efforts to block a proposed Quebec-Ontario high-speed rail line.
* **French teen loses hand in grenade blast as school protest clashes enter third week:** A 15-year-old boy lost a hand Monday near a high school in Lens after an explosion that unverified police reports said involved a stun grenade. He is hospitalized in Lille, and his life is not in danger, according to Pas-de-Calais's regional prefect.
* Police internal affairs is now handling six investigations into serious injuries during the protests; the country's Education Minister, Edouard Geffray, said Monday that 190 students have been injured since the unrest began. His ministry also noted that 589 schools were disrupted Monday, down from 735 Friday, and about 5,000 people, mostly teenagers, have been arrested since Sept. 28.
* Amnesty International France criticized the government's use of "disproportionate force" against minors during the weeks-long protests.
* **Spain 's Sanchez calls snap election for Nov. 29 after Parliament rejects housing relief measures: **Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/9ecef88a-ac63-489b-84ba-c6c6aa0aa8bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a televised address on Monday that Spain will hold a general election on Nov. 29, after Parliament rejected housing relief measures proposed by his minority government.
* The announcement follows weeks of nationwide housing protests, including a Saturday demonstration in Madrid that the government said drew more than 70,000 people, motivated in part by the televised eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid. Average rents in Spain have nearly doubled over the past decade, according to data from the Spanish real estate firm Idealista.
* The conservative People's Party, led by Alberto Nuñez Feijoo and backed by the far-right Vox party, appears poised to win in November, according to early polling. If it does, it would become the first far-right party to control the country's central government since the death of fascist dictator Francisco Franco in 1975. Sanchez has never won an outright majority but has held power for eight years across three terms.

Photo by AFP via Getty Images. Tuesday, October 6, 2026 -** Yemen : Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia activate Mecca defense pact, will deploy forces to Gulf kingdom against Houthis. Ansarallah strikes Saudi airport, Aramco refinery. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces claim capture of Mocha as coalition expands attacks on Ansarallah. Iran : U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent celebrates collective economic punishment of Iranians. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian calls U.S. negotiations "futile." U.S. President Donald Trump defends removal of U.S. bombers from UK base as seventh suspect arrested. Trump calls higher gas prices a "small price to pay" for war with Iran. Twelve sailors injured in attack on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz. Palestine : Israeli attacks kill three, wound several across Gaza. Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir joins demolition of Jerusalem apartment building as settlers torch Palestinian home, vehicles across the occupied West Bank. UK threatens to expel up to 27 Israeli diplomats over planned closure of East Jerusalem consulate. 111 Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza in September. Lebanon: Israeli airstrikes, artillery and gunfire target southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire." U.S. : Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee adds six deep-red districts to "Red to Blue" list, predicts House majority of up to 240 seats. Former President Barack Obama to campaign in Detroit with Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. Soldiers wounded in March Iranian drone strike describe medical failures, red tape, AP reports. Supreme Court opens new term with Boulder climate case against Exxon, Suncor. Trump signs order allowing the use of untaxed off-road diesel on highways. Trump approves firing squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. DOJ seeks to revoke citizenship of 40 naturalized Americans. Border agents raid Arizona protest camp, fell centuries-old cottonwood for Trump's border wall. Chicago woman shot five times by Border Patrol agent sues federal government. Trump says New York Times, other outlets should be "arrested" over coverage of Ohio rally. Texas pediatricians face investigations from Attorney General and GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton over childhood vaccinations. International: Airstrikes, artillery hit northern Ethiopia as fighting continues. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, sworn in for a new term, insists Ethiopia must have Red Sea access. ISIS attack kills Iraqi federal policeman near Kirkuk, first since U.S. withdrawal. Russian bombs kill seven, injure over 60 in Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia. Russia says Ukrainian drones struck Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, killing one. Ukraine blames Russian drones for sinking of grain ship in Romanian waters; two dead. Kuwait revokes citizenship of 415 more people, including billionaire Mahmoud Haider. Former German intelligence chief arrested on suspicion of buying classified documents for foreign spy agency. Police clash with Kosovo protesters over bid to curb Hague war crimes court. Hundreds flee RSF assaults in Sudan's Blue Nile region. Cuba says it has "channels of communication" with the U.S. but no negotiations, and is preparing to defend itself. Mexico asks the U.S. for evidence of alleged cross-border gunfire at Coast Guard personnel. Parti Quebecois wins Quebec election. French teen loses hand in grenade blast as school protest clashes enter third week. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez calls snap election for Nov. 29. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia activate Mecca defense pact, will deploy forces to Gulf kingdom against Houthis: Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Monday to activate "collective deterrence measures: under the Mecca Alliance for Defence after an emergency meeting of their defense and foreign ministers in Riyadh, the first time the pact, agreed to on August 7, has been invoked. Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman said the alliance was responding to "the heinous attacks against the Kingdom and holy sites." A separate joint statement published by the Pakistani Foreign Ministry said the three would "provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment" to Saudi Arabia under approved arrangements. Ansarallah strikes Saudi airport, Aramco refinery: Ansarallah it struck King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, disrupting air traffic, and an Aramco refinery in Rabigh, claiming to have set it on fire. It says it also hit Abha Airport, the Khamis Mushait airbase and other sites in Asir, Najran, and Jizan. The group warned all airlines to stop flying through Saudi airspace, calling it "a theater for our operations," with the exception of the airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. It said the attacks were retaliation for 60 Saudi airstrikes and a missile on Sanaa, Al-Jawf, Taiz, Hodeidah, Saada, and Marib over 24 hours, which it said killed civilians. It says 1,576 Saudi strikes have hit Yemen since the escalation began. Three people were lightly injured and infrastructure damaged in attacks on King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Jazan and Najran International Airport on Monday evening, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said. Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed Tuesday the group struck Abha International Airport in Saudi Arabia's Asir province with a ballistic missile, disrupting air traffic, though Saudi authorities have not confirmed the attack. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces claim capture of Mocha as coalition expands attacks on Ansarallah: Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces said Tuesday they had retaken the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha from Ansarallah following fighting south of the Bab al-Mandab strait, while the Saudi-led coalition announced a naval operation against Ansarallah in Hodeidah. The coalition separately said it destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Sanaa and a storage facility containing 20 ballistic missiles in Saada. Control of Mocha could provide government forces with a staging point for further operations along Yemen's Red Sea coast, though the situation on the ground remains fluid and competing territorial claims have emerged during recent fighting. Saudi-backed forces also claim to control Bab al-Mandab, an airport in Dhubab district and much of southwestern Taiz's Red Sea coastline, while Ansarallah officials say they repelled some advances and recaptured territory. Iran Bessent celebrates collective economic punishment of Iranians: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent the collapse of Iran's economy, boasting that "Operation Economic Outcast is delivering results": the rial at record lows, and zero Iranian crude loaded onto tankers last month. "The Iranian regime allows its own people to suffer," Bessent claimed, as U.S. policies punish ordinary Iranian civilians. Nurses and teachers are quitting in large numbers because their salaries no longer cover the cost of living, the New York Times reported Monday. And the U.S. blockade and sanctions have cut imports of medicine and pharmaceutical raw materials, pushing prices up and leaving pharmacies short of drugs for serious illnesses, the FT reported. Some medicines have tripled in price. Pezeshkian calls U.S. negotiations "futile": Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Monday that negotiations with the U.S. had become "futile," accusing Washington of repeatedly attacking Iran following talks and seeking to bring down the Islamic Republic. "Every time we come to the negotiating table, war is immediately imposed upon us," Pezeshkian said, according to IRNA, adding that the U.S. had attacked Iran three times following negotiations. "This demonstrates that they do not seek dialogue. On the contrary, their goal is to bring down the Islamic Republic of Iran." Trump defends removal of U.S. bombers from UK base as seventh suspect arrested: President Donald Trump on Monday defended the Pentagon's decision to remove B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in the UK following what he described as "some threats," after previously linking Iran to a security incident near the base. "Rather than tempting the enemy ... why should we leave them there? So, we moved them around a little bit. Not very far," Trump said, adding that Washington knows who made the threat and that "they've gotten themselves into big problems," without elaborating. UK counterterrorism police separately arrested a 22-year-old British national in Westminster on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts in connection with activity near Fairford, bringing the number of arrests linked to the investigation over the past two weeks to seven. Trump calls higher gas prices a "small price to pay" for war with Iran: Trump said higher gasoline prices for U.S. consumers were a "small price to pay" for what he described as keeping the U.S. and the world safe, as the war with Iran continues to disrupt energy markets. Speaking at a Republican midterm campaign rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, Trump said the price increase caused by the war was "just artificial" and "essentially almost over with," while repeating that the U.S. would not allow Iran to obtain a nuclear weapon. "They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles or San Diego. This is a very small price to pay," Trump said. He claimed gasoline prices would fall below $1.85 a gallon in "a very short period of time," potentially before or shortly after the November 3 midterm elections. Twelve sailors injured in attack on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz: Twelve sailors, including 11 Indian nationals, were injured in an attack on the Panama-flagged commercial vessel MT On Peace off Oman in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, India's Foreign Ministry said. The vessel was carrying 19 crew members, including 17 Indians. The injured sailors were evacuated with assistance from Omani authorities and are receiving treatment in Khasab. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed--one in a new Israeli attack and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and 35 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,245 killed, with 175,267 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,462 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,151, while 836 bodies have been recovered. Israeli attacks kill three, wound several across Gaza: An Israeli drone near the municipal park in central Gaza City killed one Palestinian and wounded another on Tuesday, while several Palestinians were injured in a strike on Al-Wehda Street in the west of the city, WAFA reported. In Khan Younis, an Israeli attack killed two Palestinians, according to Al Jazeera Israeli forces also shot and wounded one person in the Karama neighborhood of northwest Gaza City and another near Bir 19, south of the Mawasi area of Khan Younis. Ben-Gvir joins demolition of Jerusalem apartment building as settlers torch Palestinian home, vehicles across the occupied West Bank: East Jerusalem: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir Israeli forces during the demolition of a five-story residential building in Al-Tur containing 10 apartments and housing about 70 Palestinians, mostly women and children, on Tuesday, according to WAFA. Nablus: Israeli bulldozers agricultural land and uprooted olive trees in Iraq Burin, while blocking several village roads with earth mounds. In Aqraba, settlers torched four Palestinian vehicles and spray-painted racist slogans. Ramallah: Settlers to a home housing a family of five in Burqa, causing extensive damage. The same homeowner, a U.S. citizen, had his vehicle damaged and dozens of his olive trees cut down by settlers about a month earlier. Salfit: Settlers attempted to set fire to a poultry structure and spray-painted racist slogans on a livestock farm in Farkha. Israeli forces separately raided Salfit city and Nihad Al-Naoura, secretary of Fatah's Salfit branch. Hebron: Israeli forces Bani Naim, declared the town a closed military zone, searched several homes and converted three into military posts. UK threatens to expel up to 27 Israeli diplomats over planned closure of East Jerusalem consulate: The UK to expel one Israeli diplomat for every British diplomat forced out of Israel over Israel's plan to close the UK consulate in occupied East Jerusalem on Thursday, which could mean as many as 27 expulsions, Ynet reported. The Foreign Office declined to comment on "speculation" rather than denying the report. Israel threatened to close the consulate this week, as part of its response to the UK's ban on trade in goods from illegal West Bank settlements and sanctions on British firms aiding settlement construction. The British Foreign Office was reportedly advised by former UK attorney general Dominic Grieve that such an action would be illegal, given that the United Nations and most of its members recognize East Jerusalem as Palestinian territory. 111 Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza in September: Israeli forces 111 Palestinians in Gaza in September, including 23 children, ten women and four elderly people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry's monthly report. Israel has killed Palestinians in Gaza every month since the ceasefire began. The deadliest month was July, with 152 killed. Lebanon Israeli airstrikes, artillery and gunfire target southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire": Israeli warplanes strikes on Wadi Al-Salouqi and an area between Bra'shit and Aitaroun in the Bint Jbeil district overnight, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli artillery the outskirts of Hadatha and Bra'shit, while Israeli forces opened machine-gun fire toward Bayt Al-Sayyad and the outskirts of Mansouri. U.S. News DCCC adds six deep-red districts to "Red to Blue" list, predicts House majority of up to 240 seats: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee six candidates to its "Red to Blue" list Monday, in districts Trump won by an average of 16 points or more in 2024, signalling that the Democratic Party will allocate extra resources, and perhaps fundraising dollars, to these races. The six include: Arkansas's 2nd, where Democrat Chris Jones faces incumbent Rep. French Hill ; Colorado's 3rd, where Democrat Dwayne Romero faces incumbent Rep. Jeff Hurd ; Florida's 27th, where Eliott Rodriguez faces incumbent Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar ; New York's 21st, where Democrat Blake Gendebien faces Republican Anthony Constantino ; Nevada's 2nd, where Democrat Teresa Benitez-Thompson faces Republican David Flippo ; and Tennessee's 9th, where DemocratJustin J. Pearson faces Republican Brent Taylor. DCCC political director Brooke Butler told Politico that "anywhere between 218 and 240 feels very viable" for Democrats' potential House majority and that more seats could be added, "if gas keeps going and diesel kicks back up." Obama to campaign in Detroit with El-Sayed, Benson on Oct. 24: Former President Barack Obama will in Detroit on Saturday, Oct. 24, with Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed , gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson and other candidates, the Michigan Democratic Party announced Monday. El-Sayed faces Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers in the race to succeed retiring Sen. Gary Peters , while Benson, the secretary of state, faces Republican Rep. John James in the open governor's race. Obama has made few public stops on the trail this year but previously campaigned in Texas with Senate nominee James Talarico and gubernatorial nominee Gina Hinojosa and appeared in a campaign ad with Iowa Senate nominee Josh Turek. He is also set to headline a Washington-area fundraiser Wednesday for the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Soldiers wounded in March Iranian drone strike describe medical failures, red tape, AP reports: Nine U.S. service members in the March 1 Iranian drone strike at Port Shuaiba, Kuwait, which killed six troops on the second day of the Iran war, spoke on the record to the Associated Press about what they describe as a medical system that left them fighting for treatment on their own. Lt. Col. Arturo Linc on, who suffered shrapnel wounds to his jaw, neck, and spine, including a severed vertebral artery, was sent to barracks and told to seek outpatient appointments after Landstuhl Regional Medical Center in Germany did not admit him. Chief Warrant Officer 4 Rodney Bearman said he and others injured in the attacks were not properly registered as "wounded in combat" due to a coding error. Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom said he waited over four months for MRI results and has "had to build my own case for everything." Lincon, who still has shrapnel near his spinal cord and struggles with dizziness, told the AP that, following the attacks, in which his passport was destroyed, he was issued a temporary substitute and asked to prove his citizenship in the process (he was born in Texas to Mexican parents and graduated from West Point). He was also denied a Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance injury claim. Supreme Court opens new term with Boulder climate case against Exxon, Suncor: The Supreme Court's new term Monday with arguments in Boulder's lawsuit accusing Exxon Mobil and Suncor Energy of deceiving the public about the harms of fossil fuels. Boulder says it is seeking to recover past and future costs of repairs, emergency services and property damage, not to regulate emissions. The companies argue that only the federal government has the power to address something as large as climate change. The Trump administration has sided with them in the case. Justice Samuel Alito stepped aside a week before argument, after calls for recusal over his stock in Phillips 66 and ConocoPhillips. A 4-4 tie would leave the Colorado Supreme Court's ruling allowing the suit to proceed in place. Trump signs order allowing the use of untaxed off-road diesel on highways: President Donald Trump an executive order on Monday temporarily allowing red-dyed diesel, normally reserved for farm and industrial vehicles, to be used on highways while deferring the 24.4-cent-per-gallon federal excise tax for the rest of the year, according to a fact sheet released by the White House. Diesel prices have surged from $3.76 a gallon before the war in Iran to a record $6.53 on September 22, according to AAA. The change could potentially save truckers roughly $150 per fill-up, according to CNN, though experts noted it does nothing to improve the principal cause of rising fuel prices, a global shortage of working refineries. Trump approves firing squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan: Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell Monday on X that War Secretary Pete Hegseth "recommended" and President Trump "approved" death by firing squad for Nidal Malik Hasan , the convicted terrorist who killed 13 people and wounded 32 in the 2009 Fort Hood attack. Parnell said the Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution. At least 144 civilian prisoners have been executed by shooting since 1608, according to the AP, the most recent being South Carolina's Brad Sigmon last year, who chose the method over the electric chair and lethal injection. DOJ seeks to revoke citizenship of 40 naturalized Americans in largest denaturalization push in recent history: The Justice Department is to revoke the citizenship of 40 foreign-born Americans it accuses of lying about or omitting criminal histories on their naturalization applications, Attorney General Todd Blanche announced in a press release Monday. The government accuses the applicants of having committed crimes including espionage, transporting child pornography, sexual misconduct against a minor, and voluntary manslaughter. The cases far exceed the average of 15 a year under previous administrations. DOJ announced that it would target as many as 300 people for possible denaturalization in April. Border agents raid Arizona protest camp, fell centuries-old cottonwood for Trump 's border wall: More than 50 Customs and Border Protection agents an activist camp in Lochiel, Arizona, on Monday, ending a 70-day protest of a potential tree demolition. Following the raid, an excavator knocked down the tree, a 150-to-250-year-old cottonwood, known as the "grandmother tree," that stood in the path of President Donald Trump's $46.5 billion border wall expansion. Activists told the Washington Post that agents dragged, kicked, and knelt on protesters during a sunrise prayer ceremony, with about 10 arrested and another 10 cited. Chicago woman shot five times by Border Patrol agent sues federal government: Marimar Martinez , a Chicago woman shot five times by Border Patrol agentCharles Exum , the federal government Monday for false arrest and imprisonment, malicious prosecution, emotional distress, and negligence, with her attorneys saying an independent crime scene analysis shows the agent shot her as she turned her car away from him. Shortly after the shooting, DHS called Martinez a "domestic terrorist" and charged her, but the charges were later dropped. Exum was later placed on "administrative leave," the department noted, "consistent with policy." Martinez said she was prepared to let the matter go after charges against her were dropped, until federal agents killed two people in Minneapolis. "What's happening is not normal," she added. Trump says New York Times, other outlets should be "arrested" over coverage of Ohio rally: President Trump on Truth Social Monday that the New York Times and "many other Artificial Media Outlets, should be arrested for their dishonesty and disservice to our Country," after Times correspondent Katie Rogers reported that "several areas of an upper deck were empty" by the end of his Saturday rally at Butler High School in Vandalia, Ohio. Trump disputed the paper's claims about attendance, saying that the arena was "totally MAXED OUT" and claiming thousands were turned away at the doors. Texas pediatricians face Paxton investigations over childhood vaccinations: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , the Republican U.S. Senate nominee, a statewide investigation accusing doctors, drug companies and insurers of conspiring to push parents into vaccinating children, with a New York Times report on Monday highlighting the case of " Dr. Rachel," a central Texas pediatrician of 20 years who says responding to that investigation has cost her nearly $15,000 in legal fees and prompted her to reconsider her career. A December letter from the AG's office demanded 10 years of vaccine purchase records and her practice's vaccine policy, and said citing the CDC schedule would not suffice. In August, Paxton opened a separate probe of the American Academy of Pediatrics for "deceptively promoting childhood vaccines for financial gain." Pediatricians reject the profit motive as ludicrous, noting they pay for vaccines upfront and that nearly half of children's vaccines are covered by the federal Vaccines for Children program. Texas kindergarten measles and polio vaccine coverage has fallen to about 93 percent from nearly 97 percent in 2019. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Airstrikes, artillery hit northern Ethiopia as fighting continues after fall of Mekelle: Airstrikes at least 17 people overnight into Monday in Tigray, nine in Adwa, and eight in Sheraro, according to a humanitarian bulletin cited by Reuters, which could not confirm the reports or who launched the strikes. Government forces and fighters loyal to the Tigray People's Liberation Front also exchanged heavy artillery fire near the Tekeze River close to Mai Tsebri on Monday. In Mekelle, which Tigrayan forces left without a fight, residents said that shops were reopening and that phone and internet access was returning after a week-long disruption. Abiy, sworn in for a new term, insists Ethiopia must have Red Sea access: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Parliament Monday, as he was sworn in for another five-year term, that Ethiopia will work to secure a Red Sea port, saying "based on the principle of give and take, we will work diligently to ensure that Ethiopia has an outlet to the sea" and calling access critical to the country's "civilization." His remarks came a day after Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan, and Somalia met in New Alamein and declared that governance of the Red Sea is the "exclusive responsibility" of the region's coastal states. Eritrea has accused Ethiopia of seeking to reassert control over its coast, which it lost when Eritrea gained its independence from Ethiopia in 1993. ISIS attack kills Iraqi federal policeman near Kirkuk, first since U.S. withdrawal: At least one Iraqi federal policeman was and four wounded Monday when Islamic State militants attacked a federal police regiment near Hawija, about 70 km southwest of Kirkuk, using semi-automatic machine guns and sniper fire, two security sources told Reuters. No group has claimed responsibility, but security and army sources said ISIS militants, who retain sleeper cells in the area, were involved. It is the first reported ISIS assault on Iraqi security forces since the U.S. completed its military withdrawal from Iraq on Sept. 30. Russian bombs kill seven, injure over 60 in Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia: Three Russian bombs different areas of the northeastern Ukrainian city Kharkiv on Monday, killing six people and injuring 59, according to regional governor Oleh Syniehubov. Three of those injured in Monday's attacks on Kharkiv were children. Elsewhere on Monday, a Russian drone hit an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, injuring three people who were trapped on the ninth floor, according to that region's governor. Russian airstrikes also killed one person in Sloviansk in the Donetsk region. Russia says Ukrainian drones struck Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, killing one: Ukrainian drones a laboratory building and a radioactive waste processing facility at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant overnight on Monday, killing a driver delivering food to plant workers, according to Alexei Likhachev, head of Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom, who said there was no threat to nuclear safety. Ukraine blames Russian drones for sinking of grain ship in Romanian waters; two dead: Romania's Interior Ministry two people were killed and 11 rescued after a grain ship caught fire and sank Monday in Romania's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea; the ministry did not identify the cause of the fire. Azerbaijani and Indian nationals were reportedly aboard. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for the fire, condemning in a Monday post on X the "horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkiye." Kuwait revokes citizenship of 415 more people, including billionaire Mahmoud Haider: Kuwait six decrees published in its official gazette stripping 415 people of citizenship, including billionaire businessman Mahmoud Haider, along with dependents who obtained nationality through those whose citizenship was revoked. The Gulf state announced a citizenship review campaign in 2024, targeting fraudulent claims, including those involving individuals reporting dual nationality or those who acquired it through marriage. It has expanded this year to politicians, footballers, and musicians, including 1982 World Cup goalkeeper Ahmed al-Tarabulsi and singer Abdulmohsen Al Muhanna. Rights groups estimate at least 50,000 people have lost citizenship since 2024. Former German intelligence chief arrested on suspicion of buying classified documents for foreign spy agency: Former Federal Intelligence Service chief August Hanning was on Tuesday on suspicion of paying a former office manager at the agency for roughly 2,000 documents, including classified material and senior intelligence briefings prepared for the chancellery, and using them to draft an analysis for an officer of an unnamed foreign intelligence service, according to German federal prosecutors. Prosecutors allege the arrangement began in 2010, five years after Hanning left the agency, and that he also shared political information with a representative of a second foreign intelligence service. The office manager, identified only as Manfred D., was also arrested. The case does not involve Russia, according to the German newspaper Suddeutsche Zeitung. Police clash with Kosovo protesters over bid to curb Hague war crimes court: Police tear gas and water cannons Monday evening against several hundred protesters, including veterans and supporters of the ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army, outside Parliament in Pristina after lawmakers adjourned without passing amendments limiting the powers of the controversial Kosovo Specialist Chambers court. Twelve people were injured, including 11 civilians, according to a Pristina hospital emergency director. The amendments, which passed a first reading earlier Monday, would cap the court's sentences at 15 years, allow these to be served in Kosovo and permit appeals to Kosovo's Supreme Court. They were forwarded by the opposition Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK) and halted by Prime Minister Albin Kurti's governing Vetevendosje party. The court remains controversial in Kosovo, where the KLA, which the court was created to prosecute, is held in high esteem by many in the country's Albanian population after its fight against the Serbian-dominated Yugoslav government during Kosovo's 1998-1999 war. Hundreds flee RSF assaults in Sudan 's Blue Nile region: Hundreds of residents have the localities of Jabal Al-Nimr and Minza in Sudan's southeastern Blue Nile region after recent Rapid Support Forces attacks, the region's Humanitarian Aid Commission said on Monday. Most are heading toward the town of Al-Azaza and a settlement known as Village 6, raising concerns over civilian protection and shortages of essential supplies. Cuba says it has "channels of communication" with the U.S. but no negotiations, and is preparing to defend itself: Cuba's charge d'affaires in Washington, Lianys Torres Rivera, Reuters on Monday that Havana and Washington maintain "channels of communication"--including meetings, phone calls, and WhatsApp messages--but are not in formal negotiations and have made no progress toward restarting official talks. Rivera's remarks contradict President Donald Trump's claim last month at the UN that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was "deep into negotiations" with Havana. Torres Rivera said Cuba remains open to "respectful" dialogue with the U.S. but is "not naive" about Trump's threats and is expanding its defense preparations, saying "we are increasing our capabilities now more than ever before." She also noted that Cuba's "red line" remains changes to its political system. Mexico asks U.S. for evidence of alleged cross-border gunfire at Coast Guard personnel: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Monday her government has requested evidence from U.S. authorities about allegations that shots were fired from the Mexican side of the border at U.S. personnel, saying "we asked for all the evidence because we have no evidence" and that no National Guard, Army, or Navy personnel detected shots fired from Mexican territory toward the U.S. The comments came a day after U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson said on X that "shots were fired at U.S. Coast Guard personnel" in an area where Tamaulipas meets Texas. The incident follows Mexico's announcement of "Operation Mirror" on Sunday evening, a joint border security effort deploying 500 troops, helicopters, drones and anti-drone equipment along the frontier. Despite deepening security collaboration, Sheinbaum has repeatedly denied that her government would allow a U.S. military intervention on Mexican soil. Parti Qu ebecois wins Quebec election, complicating Carney's unity push against Trump: The separatist party Parti Quebecois, by Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, won Quebec's election Monday, according to early projections from public broadcaster Radio-Canada, though it remains too early to say whether the party secured a majority in the province's legislature. The result, widely expected before the vote, will jettison the center-right Coalition Avenir Quebec government, which has been in office since 2018. St-Pierre Plamondon has promised a referendum on leaving Canada, but only once Trump is out of the White House. Previous independence referendums failed in 1980 and 1995, and current polling puts support for a separation at around 30 percent. St-Pierre Plamondon pledged to work with Carney when it suits the province's interests; his party notably diverges from Ottawa in its calls to reduce immigration, cut Quebec's ties to the British monarchy, and efforts to block a proposed Quebec-Ontario high-speed rail line. French teen loses hand in grenade blast as school protest clashes enter third week: A 15-year-old boy lost a hand Monday near a high school in Lens after an explosion that unverified police reports said involved a stun grenade. He is hospitalized in Lille, and his life is not in danger, according to Pas-de-Calais's regional prefect. Police internal affairs is now handling six investigations into serious injuries during the protests; the country's Education Minister, Edouard Geffray, said Monday that 190 students have been injured since the unrest began. His ministry also noted that 589 schools were disrupted Monday, down from 735 Friday, and about 5,000 people, mostly teenagers, have been arrested since Sept. 28. Amnesty International France criticized the government's use of "disproportionate force" against minors during the weeks-long protests. Spain 's Sanchez calls snap election for Nov. 29 after Parliament rejects housing relief measures: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez in a televised address on Monday that Spain will hold a general election on Nov. 29, after Parliament rejected housing relief measures proposed by his minority government. The announcement follows weeks of nationwide housing protests, including a Saturday demonstration in Madrid that the government said drew more than 70,000 people, motivated in part by the televised eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid. Average rents in Spain have nearly doubled over the past decade, according to data from the Spanish real estate firm Idealista. The conservative People's Party, led by Alberto Nuñez Feijoo and backed by the far-right Vox party, appears poised to win in November, according to early polling. If it does, it would become the first far-right party to control the country's central government since the death of fascist dictator Francisco Franco in 1975. Midterms are a crucial opportunity for all of us to look inwards and think about how our vote can help future generations.
While my opponent has doubled down on the war in Iran, on tariffs and policies that take money out of the pockets of North Carolinians, I'm focused on making life easier for hardworking people that deserve a change.
As I told Lawrence on MS NOW, Washington could use a little North Carolina common sense. We have to make sure our neighbors are voting, our co-workers are voting and our family members are voting, because this is a critical time in the history of our country. If you're ready to flip the Senate and drain the swamp in Washington, I hope you'll consider [chipping in a few dollars](https://substack.com/redirect/5ac8783a-4c86-403f-8b3d-225c36d14198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [signing up to volunteer. ](https://substack.com/redirect/9a67ad99-5117-48d2-9de9-bb295f6c163d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Every effort counts.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5ac8783a-4c86-403f-8b3d-225c36d14198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Volunteer](https://substack.com/redirect/9a67ad99-5117-48d2-9de9-bb295f6c163d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
P.S. You can watch the full interview here and read the transcript below.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1d86225b-b0a9-4ef9-b717-769dddde1068?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
**Gov. Cooper:** _I appreciate your optimism, and I 'm hopeful that we can win this race and that we can take back the Senate and take back the House. We need a course correction for our country. But we know that there is a lot of big money out there, and there is a culture of DC insiders that are fueled by big money and my opponent, Michael Whatley, has been one of them for years. A lobbyist for utility companies and big oil companies._
_And the thing about it is, he has continued to do and say whatever Donald Trump has told him to do and say, regardless of whether it 's good for the people of North Carolina. So he has doubled down on the tariffs. He has doubled down on the war in Iran. He has cheered on all of these policies. And the thing about it is, he owns the stock. He owns the individual stocks of all of these companies that he's cheering for. When he cheers on the war in Iran, oil stocks go up, money goes out of the pockets of people of North Carolina and into his. When utility companies raise their rates, he owns their stock, money goes out of the pockets of the people of North Carolina and into his. And the thing about it is that they are fueling these campaigns.**People can go to[roycooper.com](https://substack.com/redirect/753ff5c0-b987-44f5-bfec-31b88569fb66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and help us out.**_
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5ac8783a-4c86-403f-8b3d-225c36d14198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_You worry about negative ads and deceptive ads that continue to lie over and over and over again. You worry about people believing it. But I 'm going to continue to hope that we can get our message out and to make sure that we are setting the record straight because people know how they feel, and they know this war in Iran is driving up gas prices. They know that these tariffs are causing them to pay more at the grocery store and whenever they buy something. And connecting those dots is really important for us right now._
**Lawrence O 'Donnell:** _One thing about both you and Sherrod Brown is that your states know you. They know you both. They 've elected you statewide before: Sherrod Brown in Ohio, you in North Carolina. Do you think that helps you survive just this carpet bombing of negative ads against you?_
**Gov. Cooper:** _That 's a really good point, Lawrence. When I left the Governor's office, I thought I might do something else. But then, when this administration took root and I saw things happening almost every single day that reached a new level of chaos, any one of which we could talk about for hours, I knew that I needed to step up and run for this Senate seat, because I knew how much money was going to come down._
_And look, I 'm going to be first in line to try and overturn Citizens United. We have to do that. But I knew that this was going to happen. I also knew that the people of North Carolina. I developed some trust with them, and I was hoping that it would take them a long time to believe negative ads that were not true, and hopefully many of them would never believe it. And I thought that that would give me an advantage, that I had the best chance to win. We haven't elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in almost two decades, and we've only elected two Democrats in almost 40 years. So that's one of the reasons why I stepped up because I knew that a lot of people were being left behind._
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5ac8783a-4c86-403f-8b3d-225c36d14198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_I saw this Washington controlled by DC insiders. I believed that Washington could use a little North Carolina common sense. I knew how to work across the aisle and get things done. Expanded Medicaid in North Carolina, 640,000 new, better-paying jobs. And I can take those receipts to Washington, and I believe I can get things done. But we 've got to get through this campaign, and we cannot stop. We all have to, across this country. We can't sit back and smile about polling leads or dissatisfaction with the president. We have to run through the tape._
_We have to make sure our neighbors are voting, our co-workers are voting, our family members are voting, because this is a critical time in the history of our country. And these midterms are a time when all of us can look inside ourselves and think this is something that I can do for future generations to make sure we make the change that we know we have to make right now._

The scent of damp earth and the heat of a turning pile signal a quiet revolution. In the compost, decay is not an end, but a profound transformation.
Just as a child mimics a parent to build soul, we must learn to mimic nature's unbreakable logic. Nature never discards; it integrates. This is the grit of the Kitchen Table--the refusal to let anything go to waste, the ability to take the broken and turn it into sustenance. To master this mimicry is to reclaim our agency, transforming the debris of our existence into the fortification of our ground.
Decomposition is the biological conversion of organic matter into nutrient-dense soil.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

## Boots on the Ground
---
| With 28 days until Election Day, Greater Georgia's ground game is in full swing.
Our team is knocking doors and making calls across the Peach State, talking directly with voters about the issues that matter to them and making sure they have the information they need before heading to the polls.
Through our voter guide, [Know Your Ballot](https://fsdy8nbbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fwVZXi3w_0RSz6fT_LYom7NHqve4KJoz7Va_j8WBPQnTsZLWnmbT-WSKLB-700Jb_dUyuAQ1dU4z-Dn41oco-jfB5Z7pQWFneBFLM62nuUPe-5viK-_MVP-0OAMPmKs5-5Mna0scdbCeX_y8z6kDE91ICLLgN32G&c=z4yAJi73cEq8LVnb-A0FMfEZnUm1M5iz-68Y9PGBDH1KsRyofXrHtA==&ch=4LGqtvlHRF8ccvXEvbUCrFKHvrrRt2LWQF7mRFzL-tIqzqeshqwbxA==), we're also helping Georgians look beyond the top of the ticket and learn more about the down-ballot candidates, offices, ballot questions, and key election dates they'll see this November.

Over the next few weeks, we'll be working to reach as many voters as possible, and we need volunteers to help us finish strong. Whether you want to knock doors alongside our team or make calls from home, even a few hours can help us reach hundreds more Georgians.
Join our team, start conversations, and help us reach voters before Election Day.

## [Know Your Ballot](https://fsdy8nbbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fwVZXi3w_0RSz6fT_LYom7NHqve4KJoz7Va_j8WBPQnTsZLWnmbT-WSKLB-700Jb_dUyuAQ1dU4z-Dn41oco-jfB5Z7pQWFneBFLM62nuUPe-5viK-_MVP-0OAMPmKs5-5Mna0scdbCeX_y8z6kDE_ZntYG_ryMj&c=z4yAJi73cEq8LVnb-A0FMfEZnUm1M5iz-68Y9PGBDH1KsRyofXrHtA==&ch=4LGqtvlHRF8ccvXEvbUCrFKHvrrRt2LWQF7mRFzL-tIqzqeshqwbxA==)
---
The races at the top of the ticket may get the most attention, but some of the offices that have the biggest impact on our everyday lives are further down the ballot. That's why Greater Georgia launched [Know Your Ballot](https://fsdy8nbbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fwVZXi3w_0RSz6fT_LYom7NHqve4KJoz7Va_j8WBPQnTsZLWnmbT-WSKLB-700Jb_dUyuAQ1dU4z-Dn41oco-jfB5Z7pQWFneBFLM62nuUPe-5viK-_MVP-0OAMPmKs5-5Mna0scdbCeX_y8z6kDE9VuXzQ7uPv3&c=z4yAJi73cEq8LVnb-A0FMfEZnUm1M5iz-68Y9PGBDH1KsRyofXrHtA==&ch=4LGqtvlHRF8ccvXEvbUCrFKHvrrRt2LWQF7mRFzL-tIqzqeshqwbxA==), a one stop shop to see who is on your ballot, what each office does, ballot questions you'll see, and key election dates you need to know.
Over the past several weeks, we've also been highlighting how these down-ballot offices connect to issues Georgians care about every day: from agriculture and public safety to education, energy, and the cost of living.
Your vote matters all the way down the ballot. Get informed before you cast it at [KnowYourBallotGA.com](https://fsdy8nbbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fwVZXi3w_0RSz6fT_LYom7NHqve4KJoz7Va_j8WBPQnTsZLWnmbT-WSKLB-700Jb_dUyuAQ1dU4z-Dn41oco-jfB5Z7pQWFneBFLM62nuUPe-5viK-_MVP-0OAMPmKs5-5Mna0scdbCeX_y8z6kDE4J5ncXPdR8q&c=z4yAJi73cEq8LVnb-A0FMfEZnUm1M5iz-68Y9PGBDH1KsRyofXrHtA==&ch=4LGqtvlHRF8ccvXEvbUCrFKHvrrRt2LWQF7mRFzL-tIqzqeshqwbxA==).

Peter,

We're officially **less than one month away** from Election Day.

That means we're officially entering the final stretch — and simply can't afford to take even a single day between now and November 3rd for granted.

Look, Wesley ran for Congress because he believes St. Louis deserves a representative who will show up, listen, and fight for the people who call this community home. And since taking office, that's exactly what he's been focused on doing.

He's worked to bring federal investments home to St. Louis, expand opportunities for workers, support our HBCUs, and make sure our community has a voice in Washington. **But Wesley also knows that the work ahead is bigger than any one district.** Right now, Republicans hold the House majority by just a handful of seats.

This November, Democrats have an opportunity to take back the House — and with it, _the ability to set a different agenda in Washington._ Over the next few weeks, our team will be working hard to reach voters, spread Wesley's message, and make sure people across the district are ready to cast their ballots. | | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/_WWv3gdC9Nm?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

name: Chris Westfall
subject: Take Action for Wildlife: Tell your senators to oppose anti-ESA legislation!
body:
New legislation would take away federal authority to review impacts on imperiled wildlife – contact your senators today!

New legislation would take away federal authority to review impacts on imperiled wildlife – contact your senators today!
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6114087/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6114088/38SyG9Xl)

SIGN NOW: Keep Threatened and Endangered Animals Protected! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6114089/38SyG9Xl)

Defender,

We’re tracking new legislation that could cut the expert scientists at the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service out of reviewing and reducing the impacts of federal projects – like data centers on public lands - on endangered animals.

This change could have a clear impact: State agencies, many of which are already underfunded, would shoulder the burden of identifying if federal projects could harm endangered species, and they’d have to decide whether and how to protect any animals at risk.

Before this legislation moves forward, your senators need to hear from you: Click here to send a message urging them to vote NO on legislation that would upend permitting authority! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6114090/38SyG9Xl)

The Endangered Species Act currently requires federal agencies to consult with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to ensure federal actions don’t jeopardize an endangered species.

The new permitting legislation would hand Fish and Wildlife Service’s authority over to state agencies. Instead of one national process, we could have a patchwork system of 50 states charged with protecting endangered wildlife without the resources or specialized knowledge they need to make informed decisions.

Here’s the kicker: One of the reasons we have the ESA today is that states couldn’t prevent many species from declining toward extinction – a federal response was needed. This legislation would put many species back in the hands of already overwhelmed state officials – and animals could start to disappear as projects move forward without sufficient review.

Before we lose the powerful tool of federal consultation under the ESA, it’s important that we speak up to keep wildlife safe. Take a moment right now to send a message to your senators urging them not to undermine permitting processes that protect our most vulnerable species!

DEEFEND AMERICA’S IMPERILED WILDLIFE! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6114091/38SyG9Xl)

Thank you for taking this important step on behalf of threatened and endangered animals.

Sincerely,

Chris Westfall

Sr. Government Relations Legislative Counsel

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

body:
People often ask...how did I get that name?

| [](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMDZfU1AtR0UuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDQ3Mzc5LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDA2X1NQLUdFLjExMDExN190MjA0NzM3OS0yMDY4In0/DIvjsGeDhxiSbEmkgB1FtA)
---
That’s a picture of me from when I flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters in the U.S. Navy. If you look to my left, you can see my call sign...**Blossom.**
People often ask...how did I get that name?
Well, my roommate in flight school and I went on a bit of a “girl power” kick one day and bought old bathtub non-skid flower stickers from the store, cut out that flower shape in reflective tape from our squadron, and stuck those reflective flowers on our helmets.
There is very little room for making a Navy flight suit more “feminine,” but on cruise we were able to be a little more creative and came to love those girly flowers on our helmets.
Although the helicopter community doesn’t use call signs as much as some of the fixed wing squadrons, the “Blossom” stuck and was painted on the side of a CH-46 for part of my first cruise. Made for a great photo and story!
It was my experience in the Navy that helped instill in me the importance of service.
Far too often, our elected officials today forget that their job is to SERVE. They think it is their job to tell everyone what to do and why everyone else is wrong....but that’s not service.
As a Navy veteran and nurse practitioner, I got so frustrated and decided to run for Congress because I wanted to actually SERVE my country and my community.
**While for some it is all about power, for me it is all about service.**
Sadly, this has made me some enemies in Washington.
No one is going to buy me off or tell me what to do...I’m going to keep serving the people I represent, not serve some “master” in Washington, D.C.
If you are also tired of leaders who care more about power than service, [I’m asking you to send me some help today.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMDZfU1AtR0UuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDQ3Mzc5LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDA2X1NQLUdFLjExMDExN190MjA0NzM3OS0yMDY4In0/Yi2iVuNxM4dPgmOnsaR88Q)
Because I’m a veteran and not a career politician, I need all the help I can get to support my fight against the Democrats.
---

It’s time we support leaders who truly want to serve our country, and that’s what I promise to always do...are you with me, Peter?
With the courage to fight,

-Jen

I buy vinyl records from Europe and Australia. For years the math worked: a €22 pressing shipped from Hamburg still beat the same record at a Nashville shop, even after Tennessee's 9.75% sales tax. Foreign supply disciplined domestic prices and kept rare catalog titles reachable.
That math is now broken -- not because records got tariffed, but because a customs rule that made small parcels frictionless is gone.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f2162f81-ef17-476c-8f10-81ed0ff2f455?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**What de minimis was**
Section 321 of the 1930 Tariff Act let goods worth $800 or less enter the U.S. duty-free with almost no paperwork. The threshold was raised to $800 in 2016, and by fiscal 2024 roughly 1.4 billion packages a year came in through it. It's the reason a one-woman Etsy shop in Lisbon or a used-record seller in Melbourne could ship to an American buyer as easily as mailing an envelope. That was the cheap-foreign-alternative engine...

body:
Caroline Kane shared your name with me. The FEC books close October 14.

Hale for Texas

Before October 14

** Let's Finish what Caroline Kane started and Make TX-07 Red Again
------------------------------------------------------------

Friend,

My name is Alexander Hale. I grew up in Houston, I live in the Heights, I work in the energy business, and I'm the Republican running to replace Lizzie Fletcher in Congress this November.

You're getting this note because Caroline Kane shared your name with me. Caroline carried our banner against Fletcher in 2024, and she was one of the first people to endorse this campaign. She knows what this seat takes, and she's been standing with us.

The deadline

One date matters more than any other between now and November 3. On October 14, the FEC pre-general reporting period closes. That report is the last public look at this race before the election, and it's the number reporters, party committees, and Fletcher's own team will use to decide whether TX-07 is in play.

| | What happens when teachers are trapped by union politics and parents are pushed aside in their children’s education? And what can citizens do when government overreach threatens their constitutional rights? This week, Debbie Kraulidis wraps up our CPAC conversations with two powerful voices for freedom. Ryan Walters, CEO of Teacher Freedom Alliance, shares how teachers can break free from union control and have a voice beyond political agendas. Then Sheriff Richard Mack explains what it means to be a Constitutional Sheriff and why understanding our rights matters when government oversteps its authority. Freedom isn't something we simply hope to preserve. We have a role to play in defending it. Tune in and discover how moms can support teachers, understand their rights, and become better equipped to stand for freedom in their own communities. Full episode available now on [YouTube](https://momsforamerica.us/so/beQ4Hv8Jv/c?w=oJ5TaNyieWdF-LPIMqDqNdTKq-YsceIdDy0bELbPOxE.), [Rumble](https://momsforamerica.us/so/beQ4Hv8Jv/c?w=WrYZBoztryTsPL6zH1wSOGTGOU797NWVvkuMzAblwIo.), [Spotify](https://momsforamerica.us/so/beQ4Hv8Jv/c?w=N9P-z-Bo3eb1ioZJ0-M6Q1Lj2O8l0zWZFigzfQ7ADwM.), and [Apple](https://momsforamerica.us/so/beQ4Hv8Jv/c?w=7Gv9cuspIL2oA_xlVEDnf67LZ_P0J8kwIzJ_NH6sKSk.).

| | Trust, but Verify

| [](https://momsforamerica.us/so/beQ4Hv8Jv/c?w=4pZHOTRYnY3P3wnlWPr88qfqPehCfjSr1y8sKTkum2I.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubW9tc2ZvcmFtZXJpY2EudXMvYmxvZyIsInIiOiI4NmYzODFiOS05YjY2LTQ3M2MtYjBkNS1lY2ZiOTIwNGVhODciLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ)

| | President Ronald Reagan famously repeated the Russian proverb, “Trust, but verify.” When it comes to your children’s education, that advice still applies. There are wonderful teachers who genuinely care about their students and academic excellence. But as parents, we cannot assume every classroom, curriculum, book, or policy reflects our values or expectations. We need to know. What is your child learning in history, math, and science? What are they being taught about sex and gender? What books are available in the classroom and library? What are the school’s policies regarding athletics, bathrooms, and parental notification? These aren't unreasonable questions. They are parental responsibilities. You have a right to know what your children are being taught. Trust your teachers. Trust your school. But verify. Read the [full blog](https://momsforamerica.us/so/beQ4Hv8Jv/c?w=ytOSqtqJNuTHXYd1RlhZkalXoqFmzkkjqS4up3YDFVs.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubW9tc2ZvcmFtZXJpY2EudXMvYmxvZyIsInIiOiIzZGQzYjI0Mi1jZmExLTQ1NjItYWJhYS1kMjgyN2JkMmIyZjMiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ) for questions every parent should be asking.

I might have one of the most demanding assignments in Washington right now.

\- I’m a freshman Congressman defending one of the most competitive seats in the country for the first time.
\- I'm a Democrat fighting to bring results to working families despite a broken, polarized Congress.
\- We flipped this district from red to blue by 653 votes.

For many in my position, that kind of intense pressure means playing it safe and doing just enough to survive the November election.

**That’s not how I'm doing things.**

I’m putting in the work in our communities. Every weekend, I'm on the ground in Orange County -- sitting down with local families, small businesses, and listening to what our neighbors actually need.
