# Early Bird Registration for the Autism Health Summit
---
|
---
| The countdown has begun for the **2027 Autism Health Summit** , taking place **April 29 through May 1, 2027** , at **The Legacy Center Resort & Spa** in **San Diego, California**. Join parents, physicians, researchers, healthcare professionals, educators, and advocates from around the world for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and hope. We're excited to announce that our **headline speakers** include **Del Bigtree** , **Dr. Henry Ealy, and Tyler Hudson** , with many more nationally recognized experts to be announced in the coming months. Attendees will gain valuable insights into the latest research, innovative therapies, integrative medicine, environmental health, and practical strategies to support individuals with autism and related neurological conditions. We're also pleased to offer **Continuing Medical Education (CME)** and **Continuing Education Unit (CEU)** credits for eligible healthcare professionals, making the Autism Health Summit an outstanding opportunity to expand your knowledge while earning valuable continuing education credits. **Now is the best time to register!** Secure your ticket before prices increase and receive **$50 OFF** your registration during the month of **October** by using promo code **AHS50** at checkout. This special offer expires at the end of the month. Whether you're a parent, caregiver, practitioner, educator, therapist, or advocate, the Autism Health Summit offers an unparalleled opportunity to learn from leading experts, connect with a passionate community, and leave empowered with practical knowledge you can apply immediately. **Reserve your seat today using the registration link below. We look forward to welcoming you to San Diego, April 29 - May 1, 2027!**

This is the perfect opportunity to showcase your organization while supporting one of the nation's premier autism education conferences.

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: Give me a freaking break
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
When Trump jokes about Iran nuking San Diego and Los Angeles, and when a bunch of his supporters defend him over it, I’m going to say something.
#

Well, Trump’s done it.
He’s gotten me to speak up for two cities in California.
There’s always a bit of a rivalry between my state and California, but at the end of the day we care about each other a lot.
So, when Trump jokes about Iran nuking San Diego and Los Angeles, and when a bunch of his supporters defend him over it, I’m going to say something.
Think about this: When Trump ordered 700 US Marines to Los Angeles last year, I’m willing to bet some of them trained in San Diego. And when Trump sent the USS Lincoln carrier group on their 320 day deployment, they set out from their home port in San Diego.
He ordered thousands of sailors and Marines based in San Diego to war, and then he joked about Iran nuking the place after they came back. This isn’t normal, Peter.
Yesterday was the last day to register to vote in Arizona. Americans in all states are getting ready to go make their voices heard, and time is running out to reach the people still on the fence.
Things like this push people further against the GOP. And over the next four weeks we need to make sure they know about it, that Trump’s the one who sent us to war, that Trump’s the reason prices are out of control and the world is in chaos.
We need Democratic majorities in the House and Senate. I’m going to be on the road until Election Day working to make that happen, and I’m asking you for your help with that.

subject: My friend Dr. Theotis Robinson Jr. is a man who has spent more than 60 years helping Tennessee live up to its promises.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY FRIENDS OF GLORIA JOHNSON, LISA SORENSEN, TREASURER
body:
We've been conspiring together for as long as I've been in politics, and this conversation is one I've been wanting to have for a long time.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/0ae13b236e18/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363923?e=dc5f639d62)

**Hey friends,** My friend Dr. Theotis Robinson Jr. is a man who has spent more than 60 years helping Tennessee live up to its promises. [**[CLICK HERE to LISTEN NOW**]](https://us.list-manage.com/yPVUdMm8ee_?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
****
[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/dqhXNcuM7HL?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

We've been conspiring together for as long as I've been in politics, and this conversation is one I've been wanting to have for a long time.Dr. Robinson grew up in segregated Knoxville, took part in the lunch counter sit-ins as a teenager, and at 18 sat down and wrote his application to the University of Tennessee the night he learned the undergraduate school didn't admit Black students. When the university said no, he told its leaders he'd sue if they didn't change the policy. They changed it, and in January 1961 he enrolled as [UT's first Black undergraduate. ](https://us.list-manage.com/8XJSQJvnDTA?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
He went on to become a vice president of equity and diversity for the UT system, and in 2019, a UT dormitory was named in his honor.
He didn't stop there. In 1969 he won a seat on the Knoxville City Council, the first Black member since 1912, and used it to push for long-overdue promotions for Black police officers and firefighters and to get Black representation on the city's boards. He's still organizing today, working to get young people out to vote and pushing back on the attacks on diversity, equity, and inclusion.We talk about what it was like growing up under segregation, what _one seat_ at the table can actually change, and why, after everything he's lived through, he says "I don't get discouraged." His message is the one we all need right now: the republic is ours to keep, but we have to show up and do the work. Early voting happens October 14-29 and Election Day is November 3rd. Make a plan to vote.
Thank you for being here,
Gloria

| | | Virginia’s Fifth District has 21 counties and 3 municipalities. At 7am yesterday, we set out to campaign across all 24 localities in 24 hours. As I write this, we are in overtime, 30 minutes from my home in Albemarle – and by the time you read this, hopefully we’ll have made it through our 24th and final stop. I know that so many people in our communities are working two jobs and then some overtime to pay their bills under Trump’s economy. So I want folks in every nook and cranny of this district to know that I am ready to fight for them, and put in the overtime to give them the representation they deserve. I am so grateful for the old and new friends we met along the 600+ mile tour of the district. I met a 100-year-old retired cattle farmer who had already voted for me, and loved my FED UP plan to support our farmers. I met a young woman who is studying at VCU to be a nurse, but had come home to vote early in Mecklenberg, because “we are finally going to have a real Representative for us.” I was blessed by a powerful interfaith prayer circle in Amelia County at 9pm, and had a ride along with Charlottesville PD at 3am. I got to deliver thank you cookies from my mother to some of our Republicans for Perriello and our Healthcare Heroes, as well as our first responders. A book club in Halifax let me crash their discussion of Walter Isaacson’s book about the Declaration of Independence, and I fed some horses in Goochland while talking to folks about how we can block Valley Link. While we covered a lot of ground, we kept coming back to the same message, the same cadence of hope and pain: Pain about the state of our country and our economy, and hope that our fellow citizens are ready to demand a better politics. **[I hope you had a chance to follow along with our 24-hour marathon. clean_body: We made it.| | | | | | | = | | | Virginia’s Fifth District has 21 counties and 3 municipalities. At 7am yesterday, we set out to campaign across all 24 localities in 24 hours. As I write this, we are in overtime, 30 minutes from my home in Albemarle – and by the time you read this, hopefully we’ll have made it through our 24th and final stop. I know that so many people in our communities are working two jobs and then some overtime to pay their bills under Trump’s economy. So I want folks in every nook and cranny of this district to know that I am ready to fight for them, and put in the overtime to give them the representation they deserve. I am so grateful for the old and new friends we met along the 600+ mile tour of the district. I met a 100-year-old retired cattle farmer who had already voted for me, and loved my FED UP plan to support our farmers. I met a young woman who is studying at VCU to be a nurse, but had come home to vote early in Mecklenberg, because “we are finally going to have a real Representative for us.” I was blessed by a powerful interfaith prayer circle in Amelia County at 9pm, and had a ride along with Charlottesville PD at 3am. I got to deliver thank you cookies from my mother to some of our Republicans for Perriello and our Healthcare Heroes, as well as our first responders. A book club in Halifax let me crash their discussion of Walter Isaacson’s book about the Declaration of Independence, and I fed some horses in Goochland while talking to folks about how we can block Valley Link. While we covered a lot of ground, we kept coming back to the same message, the same cadence of hope and pain: Pain about the state of our country and our economy, and hope that our fellow citizens are ready to demand a better politics. = If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- As the prayer circle dispersed, one of the pastors put his hand on my shoulder and said, “You must win. And you will win. We got you.” Together, we will make it so. With one stop and 28 days to go,Tom P.S. clean_body: | | Friend, There are only a few weeks left in this campaign, and I've been thinking a lot about what it takes to finish strong. It isn't one big moment. It's the steady, week-after-week work: organizers on the phones every night, volunteers knocking doors every weekend, and our message showing up on screens across NJ-09 right up until the polls close. That kind of consistency only happens when we can count on support that shows up just as consistently. That's why I'm asking you to do something that makes a real difference for us right now: = | = When you give weekly, our team can plan ahead. We know what's coming in, so we can commit to the next round of voter contact, the next canvassing shift at our headquarters, the next week of making sure people in this district hear from us and not just from the outside groups spending against us. It doesn't have to be a big amount. Even a few dollars a week, every week until November, adds up to something powerful when it's multiplied across supporters like you. = = = Thank you, Nellie | | | ---|---|--- About Nellie Pou Nellie Pou is the first Latina to represent New Jersey in Congress, and will be a target for the NRCC in 2026. As a mother and grandmother, Nellie knows what New Jersey families are facing and will continue to bring down costs while creating good-paying jobs. Nellie has dedicated her entire life to the community that raised her, and in Congress she will do the same. | = | = ---|--- Follow Nellie | | | ---|---|--- Checks may also be mailed to: Nellie Pou for Congress - PO BOX 2696, Paterson, NJ, 07509 Paid for by Nellie Pou for Congress Email is a critical way to stay in touch with our supporters, but if you wish to unsubscribe, you may do so . Case File No DRT-ED-PUMP · Special File · The Other Side of the Pump
$6.40 a Gallon. Most Drivers See a Bill. A Few Investors See a Record Margin.
Gas in California is near its all-time high, and diesel refining margins just set a record above anything in 2022. Every dollar drivers lose at the pump lands somewhere. Here’s who’s collecting it.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
California drivers are paying $6.40 a gallon for regular, a hair below the state’s all-time record. Diesel there costs $8.38. Nationally, the average is $4.43, about $1.35 above its eight-year norm. For most people, every fill-up hurts. But every dollar that leaves a driver’s wallet lands somewhere. Follow it, and you find a group of businesses having the best year in their history.
The evidence board
| | Where Your Gas Money Goes
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the pump.** As of October 1, regular gas averages $6.40 in California, $5.62 in Hawaii and $5.50 in Washington. California drivers pay about $1.75 a gallon more than a year ago, roughly $28 extra per fill-up.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the margin.** On September 1, the diesel “crack spread,” the gap between the price of crude oil and the diesel refined from it, hit a record $106 a barrel. That’s higher than anything seen in the 2022 energy crisis.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the winners.** One major refiner’s margin rose to $36.33 a barrel in the second quarter, from $17.58 a year earlier. Another roughly doubled its margin. The four biggest independent U.S. refiners just posted six straight weeks of stock gains, two of them up more than 40%.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the outlook.** Goldman Sachs expects U.S. diesel refining profits to stay near $63 a barrel into 2027, about triple normal levels.
The mechanism
| | Why Pain at the Pump Becomes Profit
---|---

---
Less supply
The Iran war has disrupted Gulf shipments. Ukrainian drones keep hitting Russian refineries. China just halted fuel exports.

Peter, Look, when I first jumped into the race to beat Mike Lawler and flip NY-17, I really didn’t know what to expect. I knew that it was going to be a hard fight. We had an initial roadmap. But a lot of it was a shot in the dark. One thing I knew for sure: I would need a massive team behind me. Now, heading into the final stretch, we've built that team. A huge chunk of our budget comes from people giving $10 or $20 to emails like this one. And with that support, we’ve built an operation that has turned this Lean-R district into a tossup. Nate Silver calls us one of three races most likely to determine control of the House. I’m incredibly proud of that, and I hope you are too. Over 250 years our nation has gone through really dark times, really hard chapters. In these extraordinary moments, ordinary people rose up and chose to live with courage. They knew America and our democracy is worth fighting for. The ending to this chapter in American history is not yet written. Who we become, the values that define us, _that is up to us._ **We are the cavalry. We are who takes this country back.** It’s up to us to beat Lawler, flip NY-17, and take back the House for Democrats. I know we can do that, but we can’t do it without you. So I’m humbly asking you to make a donation today, to help us close out the final leg of this campaign. [If I can count on your support, use this link and make a donation today. The amount is truly not as important as the donation itself. body:
Rural communities need a real voice in Congress

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140817063/651611197/-463234460?refcode=emailheader&refcode2=7607a3bb-b7c1-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ms=261006_kh_hospitals&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzYwN2EzYmItYjdjMS1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=tHEIlnI-mo-NfSKtDDcFSAUAUmwAEp5hXUT4nh-x3Fo=)

Friend, Rural communities need a real voice in Congress, and right now they don't have one. Nationally, 720 rural hospitals, roughly one-third of every rural hospital in the country, are at risk of closing due to severe financial strain caused by this reckless administration. Texas isn't just on that list. It's near the top. An estimated 55% of Texas rural hospitals are at risk of closing, with dozens considered at immediate risk. When a hospital closes, it's not just a building that shuts down. It's the nearest emergency room, the local labor and delivery unit, and often hundreds of jobs, all disappearing from a community that may not have another hospital for an hour's drive or more. This isn't happening by accident. It's happening because Washington keeps treating rural healthcare funding as an afterthought instead of a lifeline that families in districts like ours depend on. I'm running for Congress because rural communities in TX-21 deserve a representative who actually understands what's at stake when a hospital closes, not someone who's never had to worry about how far the nearest ER is. Nationally, 720 rural hospitals, roughly one-third of every rural hospital in the country, are at risk of closing due to severe financial strain caused by this reckless administration. Texas isn't just on that list. It's near the top. An estimated 55% of Texas rural hospitals are at risk of closing, with dozens considered at immediate risk. When a hospital closes, it's not just a building that shuts down. It's the nearest emergency room, the local labor and delivery unit, and often hundreds of jobs, all disappearing from a community that may not have another hospital for an hour's drive or more. This isn't happening by accident. It's happening because Washington keeps treating rural healthcare funding as an afterthought instead of a lifeline that families in districts like ours depend on. | | Dear Friend,

How much do you know about the Electoral College?

It's an important topic, and one vital to our nation's future.

You see, a movement is growing, led by progressives but supported by many well-meaning Americans, to change the way we elect our president.

**Their goal: to get rid of the Electoral College altogether, and "move beyond" the Constitution and Declaration. **

**That 's why I hope you'll take our National Quiz on Presidential Selection today.** It's a quick and engaging way to test your own understanding of how our presidents are elected.

**You can take your quiz by using the secure link below:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale-college-national-quiz-on-presidential-selection](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/i5Nq390pCRonHl9s_KtQmxcWwXSFiLLwE2QEavoowwLdYeytzynmdS2m2CRQaO6p8-ks4Rg5uVUhBNE5sCTCqLa5sfYSN4jZVZGOw9mWagDzFr5pG6hhDxNlUzv4vc2sGvYrKMACr6O3DF7nW-f2w-pheM9KMfqiZlXCuDzpGdOmyDVzfG5cdX6sy6A8Tw5OTjXrR73uzGwHmCIP1vnVns60UhCzrRIQw6izP0U6YZdiQv8OU71uWcaEoGEKgXuVmmmDMsFaYTz5EzEdL_H31-XTgB3k2RGhNESXckNO8WNxHPIZNoYOOaIU0l7YcEwTPXzcjHU33E1TsV9Wda4EiH3jlNS6QgtJe6-ElJsj_55F_Pth56CSQi0B7EoPh74aXE_WMQ2RvO9l3ElCf8LZTr9cqQfjuDY7I5GWpTp8TyNlQ2LcWSfRKRrTMvWMi1z_TT6Pqv7E5bQgcaHCe39_a72sYnBEsjNZByoR4MMrKOD_KbFU-lyQnlkZPzUHV_LoV2cHoYg-t4cVE1epUFAMzLVgIAGdF7V6NJl7LypL7161rtJrksgskw1NVBOi-hcsv08a5a7NTX8WVsvCEecmerRLc0uFJT4wqTS8a4QsWyrRheIe7rA99BpZRAbKjLLhlqOsT5UI25tfx3pk49FcNuzNJ8YYSw9gSlGd0w7Xj5pmJONyzqjcq4FBOH_YJ5sBarFyAWYVIvegHqPKEI68S_FvX0pv3tA0lKy-8xkDIEM0wJ7YCImT5HukR_-43TNvU8GO3h9iGaC9Ud2biTEnPnEHU1-BYtztaPTNe7jkPl5R6hQdYVfeL_K4S3vqtqRy0g/yJFqiEPuhmCynvKhXQXdEh-SDsNcJ9Jz/25)

For most of our history, the Electoral College was uncontroversial. It was understood to be a safeguard for free and representative government.

**But today, dozens of states have joined together to undermine this key constitutional protection.**

The push to "move beyond" the Constitution stems from the failure of too many schools to teach American civics properly. Many citizens today don't fully understand the importance of the Constitution and the Electoral College in preserving liberty.

To counter this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, **reaching and teaching millions** of Americans in all 50 states.

When you take the **National Quiz on Presidential Selection** , you'll gain a clearer understanding of how the Electoral College upholds liberty--and you'll have the opportunity to **share this** information with your fellow Americans.

So please take your **National Quiz on Presidential Selection**. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

**You can take the quiz using the secure link I 've provided below: **

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale-college-national-quiz-on-presidential-selection](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/i9omxh5KZkZdxnMIILp4U5W-5anDjlDnV4GeeneZ08jAn782G0SZrbDtOk9HblEp-VC3j4b3SkkZUnQfDwX9tBD0OD5A9IiPOjqpBP2wCRqQodA_TxjyQbv1oQBYZj2HX21qdV5rvNOY7M5WiNcXrSIsAQVQoVpvt9kcP1uD5cqB6S_tbp-31YKhrfnYocxxO-aLy4aatYMYAD-c7CVHPuTDMCHdLCXowtxTn06x_ce0SRCtCc9W1gEWQChW2IqNhb5OiBXMW3OeYKHSYxbAmIgiXbMHqgI_rLrGoy-OZ5-pt8zSHSjxpHjVV341j2rcEqwwZRsr1uzwgydPw_Kgf47DUyMgJShfw2V1S7Awp5jTq4Pe4psI6gPajknee8yuzo9kdPNx_J6fluzxGshVn11leGwSR2re349mWu3d6qqlEtgLiP-OcOdycsKIC56XGdeykbrU3M5TL80W9Wwruc20s8Ob7UmRVAa74R8foQMpkfpbkLo-gO4w0I7ylZ4I9XlsCd9l_dzNPh0Wc6g5toCanMHdDzkynVTW2x0J4UH63bOKiKDeSoonJ3XXWtBb2wPBNsNrdbY9GM-fTjy2zWypgozV2y9In8Ja6yvXOHX-V4HoZLRJXNj6QnPpAR_nC_YObhyYEyuPpofsGjh9hZKJinJf5dZFNGK_FUGYQ4fotU69AVfYZ1dQahtzfbo0aK1S9iol-6QwLt6KXVLDmS2_1uhRRK4hIirUBekxiNXrHKxdNf0Ux3tY1GCJabPDPftv0gfudcrG6KfWA9qIm7WLeQjuTKnYdovBTpqFRfSpbscBOGCvhHvSjFWat7Udow/-MPkCw0RxN0G32Qp2OOV0wn5uIA-XogH/25)

**As a thank-you for taking the quiz, I 'll send you a free 12-minute video with a Hillsdale College professor that explains the history and purpose of the Electoral College. **

The video provides a concise, engaging, and insightful overview of the Electoral College and its significance. It would be a great resource to send to a friend or a family member!

One other thing.

Hillsdale refuses EVERY PENNY of government funding--even indirectly through student loans or grants--so that we can pursue truth and defend liberty independent of meddling bureaucrats in Washington, D.C. That's why your support matters so much.

So, after you take your quiz, please also consider giving a **tax-deductible gift of $35, $50, or even $100** to help us share this video with millions of Americans--especially young people who don't understand how the Constitution preserves liberty through the Electoral College. Your gift also funds our other nationwide educational outreach.

Thank you for standing with Hillsdale College in the effort to educate Americans about the Constitution and safeguard the principles of liberty. Good luck on the quiz and enjoy your video!

Warm regards,

Bill Gray '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

**P.S.** If you know a young person who cares about civics and the Constitution, please share this email and the quiz with them! Every response helps us expand our efforts to **reach** and **teach** Americans of all ages about liberty and the Constitution. Thank you!

Dear Peter, Election Day is coming up! But for OLCV, climate action doesn’t stop when the election ends. **That’s why monthly donors are so important.** Our Sustainer Circle provides the reliable, year-round support we need to organize voters, elect climate champions, hold lawmakers accountable, and keep fighting for Oregon’s environment, even when there isn’t an election on the horizon. And we know this work makes a difference. In 2024, we helped elect a supergreen majority to the Oregon House and Senate. ORR REPORTS 6 TYPES OF UAC FRAUD AND A WEAKENED VETTING PROCESS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

The first time, the sponsor used his own identity, and the Office of
Refugee Resettlement released a 15-year-old girl to him.

Then he came back under two different aliases, with two different
identities. ORR released more children to him, and he applied for
others.

He sexually assaulted the 15-year-old and is now incarcerated,
according to ORR.

Authorities have not been able to locate a boy he sponsored under a
false name.

His case appears in the findings of a memorandum ORR published Oct. 1,
written for John Fabbricatore, ORR’s senior advisor and the former
head of ICE’s Denver field office. The document lays out six forms
of fraud in the Unaccompanied Alien Children program, and it names the
vetting policies that created the gaps.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

SOUTHWEST COLORADO HOUSING: HOUSE BILL 26-1001 LEFT PRIVATE BUILDERS
OUTSIDE THE GATE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY NAOMI RIESS, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_A GOP legislative candidate argues Colorado's housing law helps
public and nonprofit developers while leaving private builders who
could deliver attainable homes shut out of the process._

*
A LAW THAT EXCLUDES PRIVATE BUILDERS: House Bill 26-1001, signed in
March, creates a special administrative review path for housing on
properties owned by public entities or qualifying nonprofits, but the
author argues private owners willing to build affordable homes for
local workers get no similar fast-track option.

*
INFRASTRUCTURE AS THE REAL CONSTRAINT: The piece points to water and
sewer capacity limits already affecting Archuleta and San Juan
counties, arguing new development costs should fall on the projects
that create them rather than existing taxpayers, while shared-system
upgrades should be cost-shared fairly.

*
A CALL FOR TARGETED REFORM OVER MANDATES: Rather than new targets or
studies, the author, a Republican candidate for House District 59,
proposes bringing builders, utility providers and local governments
together to identify documented barriers to smaller homes, duplexes
and fourplexes, then judging success by homes actually built and
affordable.

Fellow Conservative: What's with liberals and our children? Every election cycle, Democrats tell us they're moderates. They talk about faith, decency, and "bringing people together." Then you look at the record, and you find the same thing again and again: when it comes to protecting kids, they look the other way. You've likely heard about **James Talarico** , the liberal candidate for U.S. Senate in Texas. He's a former seminarian who quotes Scripture on the campaign trail, but despite his attempts to wrap himself in Christianity, _**he voted against a bill to protect our children from sex-change surgeries, puberty blockers, and cross-sex hormones**_. So much for believing that we're all made in the image of God. Talarico even refused to oppose a bill banning sexual performances in front of minors, saying he didn't want any legislation to target the performers. He's more concerned about protecting drag queens than children in Texas. Now consider **Adam Hamilton** , the liberal candidate for U.S. Senate in Kansas. He's the founding pastor of one of the largest churches in America, and he wants Kansans to see him as a shepherd. But in November 2005, teenage boys at his church's sleep-away retreat reported that a man came into their cabin at night and touched them in their sleeping bags. A Kansas appeals court later found that camp leaders "were dismissive of their claims." The church ran its own internal review instead of calling the police. **_The next fall, the church sent the man back to the camp as a counselor._** The man was later convicted of sexual battery. Boys from Hamilton's church camp had to relive what happened to them on the witness stand. Hamilton now says he "absolutely" should have handled it differently.

Photo by Alan Shindelman
Of all the critical coverage I've seen of _Data After Dark_ so far _--_ a party I was proud to co-host and _The Compute Optimist_ proud to co-present _--_ perhaps my favorite genre is the assertion that a themed party in Washington, DC did not, in a single evening, reverse American public opinion on data centers.
As Krystal Ball of _[Breaking Points](https://substack.com/redirect/167a11f6-87c5-414c-b2de-0cb05b15bc59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ put it, she "can't imagine a single rural American" who would be persuaded because "some people in DC had a cocktail party." Her co-host, Saagar Enjeti, added, "Generally, just some advice, that's not really how you move the needle."
The Compute Optimist is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..lXf2vSmiZCY7BarRBWYlKuhvQIzj6m012CTjl5G8JUU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=218397710)
I appreciate the advice, Saagar, and I'm glad we can at least agree that, as you mentioned on the show, in-person socialization is _good_. But the value of the party was never that people would hear about a pro-data center party in the nation's capital and suddenly see the light on the importance of the data center buildout. Nor have we ever argued that data centers belong anywhere and everywhere.
The value of _Data After Dark_ lies in something much deeper.
What started as two friends and me planning a themed house party quickly grew into something far bigger. Within about an hour, my co-hosts [Jonas Du](https://substack.com/redirect/c24d4488-4c51-4279-bab6-73034312223c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Casey Given](https://substack.com/redirect/3d71fcc8-5a33-4b3f-b561-a104309c5ce2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and I posted _Data After Dark_ on _Partiful_. By morning, about 100 of our friends had RSVP'd.
In the weeks and months leading up to that night, anti-data center fervor had reached a breaking point. Strikingly, a _Gallup_ [poll](https://substack.com/redirect/78e2e162-c9e0-4b05-b062-50419b87713a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) had found seven in ten Americans opposing the construction of "data centers for artificial intelligence in their local area." Politicians, sensing the changing winds, were quick to respond.
The data center debate was something the three of us had all discussed with our friends countless times, and with great frustration. In my experience, much of the opposition is being driven by false or exaggerated claims, but not all of it. Many are also asking valid community questions, and tech companies will have to make their case in those towns. The issue? Whether rooted in legitimate concerns or misconceptions, many of these objections can be addressed through better information or technological solutions. Yet data center opposition was increasingly fueling support for radical and reactionary proposals like all-out moratoriums.
The first statewide data center moratorium was [signed](https://substack.com/redirect/79f57f7a-450c-4565-b982-3d58a7b5f770?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this summer, support for Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders' [national moratorium](https://substack.com/redirect/02464965-2c4c-4697-81b4-ee3452d8fb2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [expanded](https://substack.com/redirect/e7270966-da86-43e1-8fcf-bed49121e6fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) beyond its niche progressive origins to include a powerful committee ranking member, and midterm [campaign ads](https://substack.com/redirect/bb21ab59-c50d-45ba-8227-67d04ff352ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) were increasingly using past support for data center projects as a political weapon.
On August 20, I [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/a0fcd05e-6f67-4040-957b-b371d81c1daa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) my frustration on _X_ : "If not, in 30 years, we'll be watching documentaries about how the Jane Fondas of today destroyed our standing as the world's compute superpower. People will so obviously realize how wrong they were today." This was a callback to watching documentaries with my dad as a kid detailing the history of nuclear energy in America. Collectively, those documentaries led me to discover that something I'd opposed out of fear and pessimism wasn't what I thought it was.
Fear and pessimism are the right words. Fear of the unknown and pessimism about what emerging technologies could mean for the future. It's a tale as old as time, with America's data center and broader AI buildout as the latest iteration.
The _exhaustion_ with the prevailing climate of fear and pessimism is, in my view, the spark that made _Data After Dark_ go viral. When Jonas and I posted the party on _X_ , we were having fun with it. And we both knew those exhausted by the constant and growing negativity surrounding what they understand to be critical infrastructure would get a kick out of the themed party. We just didn't realize _quite_ how much of a kick.
With the screenshot of the _Partiful_ invite, Jonas [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/03efbdd8-7022-4b72-9234-53ad2ef7d275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "Who wants to come to my pro-data center party in DC" to which I immediately [reposted](https://substack.com/redirect/e5027b16-b99d-4336-8b70-615c018bd440?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with "Yes, we're hosting a pro-data center party in DC next month... Yes, we will be serving Loudoun County Ice Teas." It didn't take long for both posts to catch fire, with Jonas's post drawing more than 322,000 views and mine more than 52,000.
"Based on the replies this is becoming the event of the season," [said](https://substack.com/redirect/d83c0a29-0f83-4b4b-9899-ce8b4ea76f25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Taylor Lorenz. "lfg. I'm there," [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/e5027b16-b99d-4336-8b70-615c018bd440?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) @/ira_quint. "Flying back to DC for this," [stated](https://substack.com/redirect/f2eb9bbe-703c-4ae0-ab2a-8578d18e39ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Nahom Sisay.
It quickly became clear that Jonas's 900-square-foot DC row house, where we initially planned to co-host the party, was not going to fit everyone who wanted to come.
Among the responses were tech startup builders and nonprofits graciously jumping in to offer their support. We had clearly tapped into something, and they wanted to make sure capacity wouldn't keep it confined to a row house.
That something was a yearning for optimism. AI is poised to deliver immense value for humanity, and those who recognize it are increasingly fatigued not only by the continuing proliferation of fear-based doomerism, but by how open excitement about technological progress is often met with scolding and unfounded accusations ranging from disregarding the environment to "shilling for big tech." In a way, for many, that optimism was becoming a form of rebellion.
"It really is our generation's Industrial Revolution, but bigger," I [told](https://substack.com/redirect/2c80bd35-e141-41c8-82d6-2808a7759402?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) VICE in an interview about the party last week. "The risk of slowing down is far greater than pushing forward." And this is the greater point. In throwing this party, our message was simple: _You 're allowed to be excited and optimistic about the remarkable and innovative things happening in American tech right now._ What _Data After Dark_ revealed was that the doomers do not have a monopoly on the energy and sentiment toward tech. There is a robust constituency for techno-optimism, and that constituency is hungry to express it.
The tech and politico worlds came together in a novel way that Saturday night: not over stuffy Hill meetings, rubber-chicken dinners, or a name-tagged networking event, but in the whisky lounge, over live jazz, and while dancing under a flag with the words "Come And Take It" beneath the image of a data center server.
While the typical DC crowd was certainly represented, _Data After Dark_ was far from limited to it. I should know--I organize monthly happy hours and policy panels in the city. It enabled communicators, policy wonks, and startup builders to converge outside the usual professional circles. Not merely to "network," but to get to know one another, celebrate optimism for the future, and yes, _have fun_.
No one in that room needed convincing that data centers have a PR problem. What they needed was to know one another. Professionals approaching the issue from different parts of the tech and policy worlds, who might otherwise never have met, are now acquainted. And from my conversations with friends, old and new, those relationships are already continuing and evolving beyond the party.
Finally, while much of the media coverage carried a negative flavor, the party provided a platform for getting out our message about optimism and innovation. If the SMRtini, named after small modular reactors (SMRs) to highlight one answer to data center grid concerns, or the Closed-Loop Spritz, named after closed-loop cooling systems to highlight how innovation is enabling data centers to recycle and reuse water, prompted even one conversation about these solutions, I'd call that a win. And when it came to optimism, one moment captured the contrast perfectly.
The protesters who stormed the stage put the divide between optimism and pessimism on full display. When the crowd broke into chants of "USA!" in response, I quickly joined my friend Jonas on the stage to help carry the chant. Photos and videos captured the two of us holding the microphone, smiling, laughing, and chanting alongside the crowd. Next to us, a protester shouted back at the attendees, at one point giving them the finger.
And that's the contrast. The techno-optimists are _having fun_. And optimism is how we win.
_Ed Tarnowski is the Founder and Editor of The Compute Optimist. He is also a Resident Fellow, Technology and Innovation at the R Street Institute, a Senior Contributor at Young Voices, and the Washington, DC Regional Director for America 's Future. All opinions expressed are his own._

What Data After Dark was really about--and the media misunderstanding | | | Oct 5 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Photo by Alan Shindelman Of all the critical coverage I've seen of Data After Dark so far -- a party I was proud to co-host and The Compute Optimist proud to co-present -- perhaps my favorite genre is the assertion that a themed party in Washington, DC did not, in a single evening, reverse American public opinion on data centers. As Krystal Ball of put it, she "can't imagine a single rural American" who would be persuaded because "some people in DC had a cocktail party." Her co-host, Saagar Enjeti, added, "Generally, just some advice, that's not really how you move the needle." The Compute Optimist is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. I appreciate the advice, Saagar, and I'm glad we can at least agree that, as you mentioned on the show, in-person socialization is good. But the value of the party was never that people would hear about a pro-data center party in the nation's capital and suddenly see the light on the importance of the data center buildout. Nor have we ever argued that data centers belong anywhere and everywhere. The value of Data After Dark lies in something much deeper. What started as two friends and me planning a themed house party quickly grew into something far bigger. Within about an hour, my co-hosts , , and I posted Data After Dark on Partiful. By morning, about 100 of our friends had RSVP'd. In the weeks and months leading up to that night, anti-data center fervor had reached a breaking point. Strikingly, a Gallup had found seven in ten Americans opposing the construction of "data centers for artificial intelligence in their local area." Politicians, sensing the changing winds, were quick to respond. The data center debate was something the three of us had all discussed with our friends countless times, and with great frustration. In my experience, much of the opposition is being driven by false or exaggerated claims, but not all of it. Many are also asking valid community questions, and tech companies will have to make their case in those towns. The issue? Whether rooted in legitimate concerns or misconceptions, many of these objections can be addressed through better information or technological solutions. Yet data center opposition was increasingly fueling support for radical and reactionary proposals like all-out moratoriums. The first statewide data center moratorium was this summer, support for Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders' beyond its niche progressive origins to include a powerful committee ranking member, and midterm were increasingly using past support for data center projects as a political weapon. On August 20, I my frustration on X : "If not, in 30 years, we'll be watching documentaries about how the Jane Fondas of today destroyed our standing as the world's compute superpower. People will so obviously realize how wrong they were today." This was a callback to watching documentaries with my dad as a kid detailing the history of nuclear energy in America. Collectively, those documentaries led me to discover that something I'd opposed out of fear and pessimism wasn't what I thought it was. Fear and pessimism are the right words. Fear of the unknown and pessimism about what emerging technologies could mean for the future. It's a tale as old as time, with America's data center and broader AI buildout as the latest iteration. The exhaustion with the prevailing climate of fear and pessimism is, in my view, the spark that made Data After Dark go viral. When Jonas and I posted the party on X , we were having fun with it. And we both knew those exhausted by the constant and growing negativity surrounding what they understand to be critical infrastructure would get a kick out of the themed party. We just didn't realize quite how much of a kick. With the screenshot of the Partiful invite, Jonas "Who wants to come to my pro-data center party in DC" to which I immediately with "Yes, we're hosting a pro-data center party in DC next month... Yes, we will be serving Loudoun County Ice Teas." It didn't take long for both posts to catch fire, with Jonas's post drawing more than 322,000 views and mine more than 52,000. "Based on the replies this is becoming the event of the season," Taylor Lorenz. "lfg. I'm there," @/iraquint. "Flying back to DC for this," Nahom Sisay. It quickly became clear that Jonas's 900-square-foot DC row house, where we initially planned to co-host the party, was not going to fit everyone who wanted to come. Among the responses were tech startup builders and nonprofits graciously jumping in to offer their support. We had clearly tapped into something, and they wanted to make sure capacity wouldn't keep it confined to a row house. That something was a yearning for optimism. AI is poised to deliver immense value for humanity, and those who recognize it are increasingly fatigued not only by the continuing proliferation of fear-based doomerism, but by how open excitement about technological progress is often met with scolding and unfounded accusations ranging from disregarding the environment to "shilling for big tech." In a way, for many, that optimism was becoming a form of rebellion. "It really is our generation's Industrial Revolution, but bigger," I VICE in an interview about the party last week. "The risk of slowing down is far greater than pushing forward." And this is the greater point. In throwing this party, our message was simple: You 're allowed to be excited and optimistic about the remarkable and innovative things happening in American tech right now. What Data After Dark revealed was that the doomers do not have a monopoly on the energy and sentiment toward tech. There is a robust constituency for techno-optimism, and that constituency is hungry to express it. The tech and politico worlds came together in a novel way that Saturday night: not over stuffy Hill meetings, rubber-chicken dinners, or a name-tagged networking event, but in the whisky lounge, over live jazz, and while dancing under a flag with the words "Come And Take It" beneath the image of a data center server. While the typical DC crowd was certainly represented, Data After Dark was far from limited to it. I should know--I organize monthly happy hours and policy panels in the city. It enabled communicators, policy wonks, and startup builders to converge outside the usual professional circles. Not merely to "network," but to get to know one another, celebrate optimism for the future, and yes, have fun. No one in that room needed convincing that data centers have a PR problem. What they needed was to know one another. Professionals approaching the issue from different parts of the tech and policy worlds, who might otherwise never have met, are now acquainted. And from my conversations with friends, old and new, those relationships are already continuing and evolving beyond the party. Finally, while much of the media coverage carried a negative flavor, the party provided a platform for getting out our message about optimism and innovation. If the SMRtini, named after small modular reactors (SMRs) to highlight one answer to data center grid concerns, or the Closed-Loop Spritz, named after closed-loop cooling systems to highlight how innovation is enabling data centers to recycle and reuse water, prompted even one conversation about these solutions, I'd call that a win. And when it came to optimism, one moment captured the contrast perfectly. The protesters who stormed the stage put the divide between optimism and pessimism on full display. When the crowd broke into chants of "USA!" in response, I quickly joined my friend Jonas on the stage to help carry the chant. Photos and videos captured the two of us holding the microphone, smiling, laughing, and chanting alongside the crowd. Next to us, a protester shouted back at the attendees, at one point giving them the finger. And that's the contrast. The techno-optimists are having fun. And optimism is how we win. Peter, Donald Trump spent yesterday musing at a campaign rally about "allowing" Iran to unleash nuclear weapons against American cities. It's the kind of remark that would spark outcry and demands for impeachment, invoking the 25th amendment, anything to remove this unhinged madman from power. Instead this madman has his finger on our own nuclear weapons - and the generals and admirals who might challenge an impulsive, reckless, dishonorable and unlawful order have been gutted from our ranks one by one. Last week, Secretary of "War" Pete Hegseth bragged that one in five of America's generals and admirals have been removed. He fired 10% outright for a host of dubious reasons, and abolished another 10% of the positions waiting to be filled with experienced officers. The press rightly described it as an unprecedented purge of military leadership. Hegseth called it "accountability." _Accountability._ **This from the least qualified Secretary of Defense in American history, a likely war criminal from the Minab school massacre who is massively outranked and out-classed by every single officer he 's fired without cause.**

clean_body: Hegseth should be facing a tribunal. Instead he is firing generals. | | Peter, Donald Trump spent yesterday musing at a campaign rally about "allowing" Iran to unleash nuclear weapons against American cities. It's the kind of remark that would spark outcry and demands for impeachment, invoking the 25th amendment, anything to remove this unhinged madman from power. Instead this madman has his finger on our own nuclear weapons - and the generals and admirals who might challenge an impulsive, reckless, dishonorable and unlawful order have been gutted from our ranks one by one. Last week, Secretary of "War" Pete Hegseth bragged that one in five of America's generals and admirals have been removed. He fired 10% outright for a host of dubious reasons, and abolished another 10% of the positions waiting to be filled with experienced officers. The press rightly described it as an unprecedented purge of military leadership. Hegseth called it "accountability." Accountability. This from the least qualified Secretary of Defense in American history, a likely war criminal from the Minab school massacre who is massively outranked and out-classed by every single officer he 's fired without cause. Count how many times I have had to write to you about this man, and count the wreckage behind each update. Troops eating battlefield rations in the seventh month of his illegal war because he recklessly underestimated the consequences of starting a protracted armed conflict on the doorstep of dozens of American military bases. A leadership corps so hollowed out that his Pentagon walked into the worst-case scenario: both of the world's critical oil chokepoints closed at once. All while you pay for it at the pump. He’s hidden our war casualties from the public rolls and forced a widow to fight for benefits her husband paid for with his blood. Now he is cutting leadership again because firing men and women who spent decades earning stars he never came within a mile of exposes him as dangerously unqualified for the job. But this is not just about Pete Hegseth. The mandate to slash and consolidate military leadership – and test them for their loyalty to Trump – is straight out of Project 2025. Concentrate power in the executive, remove every officer with the standing to object, and leave nobody between an abusive administration and the orders it wants followed. Conscientious objector claims are surging among active-duty troops, with some advocates reporting a 1000% increase since the Minab school massacre. And veterans who studiously avoid speaking out against a sitting administration – to preserve the military’s important function of political neutrality – are speaking up in record numbers. Hegseth’s tenure at the Pentagon has led to an unprecedented collapse of morale; widespread destruction of critical military infrastructure; and long-term damage to our military readiness. His conduct in office is unforgivable. But it cannot be unaccountable. Our constitution empowers Congress to impeach and remove any political appointee who has abandoned their oath as Hegseth has done. subject: Who will you be for the next four weeks?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Michaela for Tennessee [www
body:
We’re exactly one month out from the November 3 election, which means...
---
| |
---
|
---
Everyone said it was too early back in February. We were focused on the local elections in April. We celebrated the school board flip in August. The last day to register to vote in the midterms was _yesterday._ It's time. **There are two types of members of this movement, and you get to be one or both. ** You are either the person knocking doors, calling voters, writing postcards, and making sure people know about this campaign, or you are the person funding those efforts. **For the next four weeks, we need to knock another 20,000 doors, send another 200,000 text messages, and put up even more ads on social media AND streaming platforms. ** To win this election, it's going to take ALL OF US contributing our time, effort, creativity, and cash to reach our most disenfranchised neighbors. Hey Peter – it’s Vivek Ramaswamy.
I know you're passionate about saving America - I am too.
We are in the middle of a battle for the soul of this country, and let me be clear: [The race for Governor here in Ohio is going to be one of the biggest battles in the entire nation this year.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTEmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYxMDA2X1NLLTczLjExMDExN190MjA0NzI5OC0zNjIzJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MTAwNl9TSy03My4xMTAxMTdfdDIwNDcyOTgtMzYyMyJ9/JvNpGl6z5Nuw0xkNz-JEzg)
[That's why I'm humbly asking you to invest in my must-win campaign right now.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTEmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYxMDA2X1NLLTczLjExMDExN190MjA0NzI5OC0zNjIzJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MTAwNl9TSy03My4xMTAxMTdfdDIwNDcyOTgtMzYyMyJ9/dbk8I3P-Y3vGINMVx5kErA)
I'm not asking for a huge donation... [I’m asking you to chip in just $1 today - seriously. ](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTEmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYxMDA2X1NLLTczLjExMDExN190MjA0NzI5OC0zNjIzJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MTAwNl9TSy03My4xMTAxMTdfdDIwNDcyOTgtMzYyMyJ9/U34Gjl34ZCp7-lUpCCjuDw)
When thousands of grassroots patriots from every corner of this country invest just one dollar, it sends a message the Democrat Machine cannot ignore, or match.
[Your $1 investment](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTEmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYxMDA2X1NLLTczLjExMDExN190MjA0NzI5OC0zNjIzJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MTAwNl9TSy03My4xMTAxMTdfdDIwNDcyOTgtMzYyMyJ9/3C8ywUuEQgarGR4jCgwT0Q) is a declaration of independence from the failed policies of the past.
[Your $1 investment](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTEmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYxMDA2X1NLLTczLjExMDExN190MjA0NzI5OC0zNjIzJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MTAwNl9TSy03My4xMTAxMTdfdDIwNDcyOTgtMzYyMyJ9/DE5v-gtSwNO66M6ONl2NMQ) is an endorsement of the future our campaign is fighting for:
* Slash taxes and lower prices – you earned your nest egg, you should keep more of it
* Overhaul failing schools – I’ll expand school choice and reward excellent teachers
* Restore national identity – we’ll promote merit and patriotism, and reject victimhood
* Deport every illegal alien – Tom Homan is a hero, he’ll have a direct line to my office
* Roll back transgenderism – ban men in women’s sports, no sex changes for minors
* Gut all DEI programs in the state – we’ll be a model for rooting out woke propaganda
* Secure elections and prosecute fraud – our elections will be the safest in the country
* Obliterate the managerial bureaucracy – I’ll take a hacksaw to government bloat

[Whether you live in Ohio or not, will you invest just $1 (or more if you can swing it) today?](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTEmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYxMDA2X1NLLTczLjExMDExN190MjA0NzI5OC0zNjIzJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MTAwNl9TSy03My4xMTAxMTdfdDIwNDcyOTgtMzYyMyJ9/aHHbIMGn-JviygxjGMBQnw)
Not just to hit a goal, but to send a message: You’re with us. You believe in this movement. And you’re ready to fight.
[Every dollar you chip in helps](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTEmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYxMDA2X1NLLTczLjExMDExN190MjA0NzI5OC0zNjIzJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MTAwNl9TSy03My4xMTAxMTdfdDIwNDcyOTgtMzYyMyJ9/crBf7shpdhPoCpWQVS1jZA) me build the kind of grassroots army it will take to win the most important race in America this November.
God bless you, Vivek Ramaswamy

The political forecasters now give Democrats a 75 percent chance of taking back the House. | | Friend,

The political forecasters now give Democrats a 75 percent chance of taking back the House. Just last week, the Cook Political Report moved fifteen more races in the Democrats' direction. Even friendly analysts say the floor is falling out from under House Republicans.

Taliban military vehicles parade to celebrate the third anniversary of Taliban's takeover of Afghanistan, at the Bagram Air Base, on August 14, 2024. Photo by Ahmad Sahel Arman/AFP via Getty Images.
BAGRAM, Afghanistan-- "They are back," said Abdul Maroof, a 38-year-old resident of Kabul. "God knows what they are doing, but they are back and the Taliban are hiding it."
Maroof had not been to Bagram himself. Like many in the capital, he heard the story from friends, relatives, and social media feeds insisting that foreign military vehicles and low-flying aircraft had been spotted near the perimeter. In Kabul, where political anxiety fuels a relentless rumor mill, the claim is repeated as settled fact. For months, viral videos and online commentary have alleged that U.S. forces quietly reclaimed the sprawling airfield north of the capital--or that the Taliban now manage it under a secret pact with Washington.
In Bagram itself, the story dissolves.
"I heard about these rumors," said Abdul Latif, 60, a lifelong resident of the area. "Relatives called me from all over asking if the Americans were back. But it's not true. I was here when the first Americans arrived in 2001. Nothing like that is happening now."
Every local around the base's perimeter and adjacent bazaars offered the same account: the only armed men entering and leaving are Taliban fighters. There are no foreign contractors and no Americans. Like Latif, residents report that their phones have been ringing continuously with calls from family members across Afghanistan and throughout the diaspora--all seeking confirmation of the same viral reports. The answer from the gates remains identical: nothing is happening here.
Yet while locals dismiss rumors of an American return, the skies over Bagram have not remained entirely quiet. In late February and early March 2026, amid a violent cross-border escalation between Islamabad and Kabul, Pakistani airstrikes targeted the facility. The Taliban regime claimed its air defense systems intercepted the attack, while local reporting and satellite imagery suggested strikes hit outer sections of the installation. For residents living at the base's edge, the strikes were a sharp reminder that even without American boots on the ground, Bagram remains a target on the regional chessboard.
What was once the logistical heart of the U.S.-led War on Terror now sits under a heavy, precarious silence. Bagram Air Base's military lineage runs deep. Built with Soviet assistance in the 1950s--when Washington and Moscow competed for influence in non-aligned Kabul--it became the primary staging hub for the Soviet Army's brutal occupation in the 1980s, launching airstrikes and combat missions across the countryside. Following the Soviet withdrawal, the base was repeatedly contested during the civil war of the 1990s, eventually becoming a fortified front line between the Taliban and the Northern Alliance.
After late 2001, U.S. forces and their NATO allies transformed Bagram into a massive, heavily fortified garrison. At its peak, it housed tens of thousands of personnel, operating like an isolated American suburb complete with paved avenues, fitness centers, and fast-food chains like Burger King and Pizza Hut. A short distance from these amenities stood the Bagram theater internment facility, where thousands of Afghans were held without trial for years, and where severe prisoner abuse and torture were systematically documented. Bagram also served as a focal point for broader covert networks, linking into nearby CIA dark sites such as the Salt Pit, where detainees were subjected to brutal interrogation methods, including beatings, prolonged isolation, exposure to extreme cold, and other forms of torture.
## A Base Washington Wants Back
The persistence of the rumors of an American return relies partly on the base's current opaqueness. Over the past two years, security and access around the facility have tightened significantly.
During my visit to Bagram, I was accompanied by an officer from the Taliban's intelligence service, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. He dismissed claims of a foreign troop presence outright.
"It is all fake news," he said. "We control the entire base. No Americans are here, and we would never tolerate a foreign military presence in Afghanistan. That is why we fought them for twenty years."
Yet when he attempted to enter the base with me, guards turned us away. Even with his credentials, he could not cross the perimeter.
"Unfortunately, it is out of our hands," he admitted. "The Ministry of Defense decides who enters."
This compartmentalization of authority has continued to fuel domestic suspicions about the site.
Strategic interest in Bagram, meanwhile, remains active abroad. In September 2025, President Donald Trump stated publicly that the United States should seek to regain control of Bagram, citing its strategic proximity to Chinese and Iranian borders. Situated in Parwan Province, Bagram offers a prime location to carry out surveillance operations in Central Asia, Iran, Pakistan, and western China. Local residents noted that for years, many residents assumed Washington would never abandon an asset of such strategic value.

Food vendors outside the Bagram Air Base, on Sept. 10, 2026. Photo by Emran Feroz for Drop Site News.
## War Memories
For many living near the base, the departure of foreign forces marked the collapse of the local economy.
"Business was good when the Americans were here," said Mohammad Musa, 18, who runs a shop with his family near the base gates. "There were so many people buying goods every day."
Under the foreign military presence, a complex ecosystem of primary contractors, subcontractors, and service providers injected significant capital into the surrounding villages. While the political and human costs of the war were severe, the financial ecosystem provided livelihoods for thousands of local families.
"We worked and we could feed our families," Abdul Latif said, speaking openly despite the presence of Taliban intelligence personnel nearby. "For us, that part was not bad."
The accompanying officers listened to these statements without intervening or penalizing the speakers, though they occasionally countered with official regime rhetoric regarding national sovereignty and victory over foreign occupation.
These interactions reflect a nuanced reality of the conflict: for those living in its immediate radius, the foreign presence was not experienced solely through the lens of military occupation, but also as a commercial opportunity. Five years into Taliban governance, remnants of that economic dependence linger in local memory.
For others, Bagram remains defined by the systemic abuses that took place inside its prisons.
Throughout the war, the base's detention center operated largely outside international legal oversight. Detainees were held for years without charge or legal representation. Notable instances of fatal abuse, including the 2002 deaths of Afghan detainees Dilawar and Habibullah at the hands of U.S. personnel, were documented in subsequent military investigations and investigative reports.
Mufti Abdul Ahad Hakimi, now a high-ranking Taliban official, spent several years imprisoned at Bagram during the war.
"I was tortured by both American soldiers and their Afghan counterparts," Hakimi said, describing prolonged physical and psychological pressure aimed at forcing him to switch political loyalties. "They wanted us to accept their system. I refused."
Hakimi was eventually released as part of the large-scale prisoner exchanges conducted under the administration of President Ashraf Ghani following the February 2020 U.S.-Taliban agreement signed in Doha. Many of those who served prison terms there during the war and suffered torture at the hands of U.S. and Afghan government troops had no ties to militant groups.
"The majority of the people detained in Bagram were not combatants," he said. "They were ordinary civilians swept up in raids because they lived in active zones or had loose ties to prominent figures."
For Hakimi, the collapse of the Afghan republic in August 2021 marked a complete reversal: "When August 15 came, we returned to Bagram not as prisoners, but as its liberators."
## Who Is Inside Now?
Bagram's legacy as a prison facility has generated a second set of rumors about its current role. Reports across Afghanistan suggest that the Taliban are utilizing the facility to hold criminal suspects, alleged members of Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP), and political dissidents.
Hakimi acknowledged that parts of the facility remain operational under the Ministry of Defense, though he declined to specify the number of detainees, their identities, or the legal standards governing their detention.
Outside the walls, daily routines around the Bagram bazaar continue uninterrupted between moments of tension. Convoys of Taliban vehicles occasionally pass through the outer gates, but the surrounding district remains quiet. For two decades, Bagram existed as a high-security enclave of foreign military power; today, those living beside it find themselves navigating both the legacy of that presence and the lingering threat of a new regional conflict.
"It was completely different back then," said Mohammad Musa from his shop near the road. "Now, everything has gone quiet."

The Taliban regime claimed its air defense systems intercepted the attack, while local reporting and satellite imagery suggested strikes hit outer sections of the installation. For residents living at the base's edge, the strikes were a sharp reminder that even without American boots on the ground, Bagram remains a target on the regional chessboard. What was once the logistical heart of the U.S.-led War on Terror now sits under a heavy, precarious silence. Bagram Air Base's military lineage runs deep. Built with Soviet assistance in the 1950s--when Washington and Moscow competed for influence in non-aligned Kabul--it became the primary staging hub for the Soviet Army's brutal occupation in the 1980s, launching airstrikes and combat missions across the countryside. Following the Soviet withdrawal, the base was repeatedly contested during the civil war of the 1990s, eventually becoming a fortified front line between the Taliban and the Northern Alliance. After late 2001, U.S. forces and their NATO allies transformed Bagram into a massive, heavily fortified garrison. At its peak, it housed tens of thousands of personnel, operating like an isolated American suburb complete with paved avenues, fitness centers, and fast-food chains like Burger King and Pizza Hut. A short distance from these amenities stood the Bagram theater internment facility, where thousands of Afghans were held without trial for years, and where severe prisoner abuse and torture were systematically documented. Bagram also served as a focal point for broader covert networks, linking into nearby CIA dark sites such as the Salt Pit, where detainees were subjected to brutal interrogation methods, including beatings, prolonged isolation, exposure to extreme cold, and other forms of torture. A Base Washington Wants Back The persistence of the rumors of an American return relies partly on the base's current opaqueness. Over the past two years, security and access around the facility have tightened significantly. During my visit to Bagram, I was accompanied by an officer from the Taliban's intelligence service, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. He dismissed claims of a foreign troop presence outright. "It is all fake news," he said. "We control the entire base. No Americans are here, and we would never tolerate a foreign military presence in Afghanistan. That is why we fought them for twenty years." Yet when he attempted to enter the base with me, guards turned us away. Even with his credentials, he could not cross the perimeter. "Unfortunately, it is out of our hands," he admitted. "The Ministry of Defense decides who enters." This compartmentalization of authority has continued to fuel domestic suspicions about the site. Strategic interest in Bagram, meanwhile, remains active abroad. In September 2025, President Donald Trump stated publicly that the United States should seek to regain control of Bagram, citing its strategic proximity to Chinese and Iranian borders. Situated in Parwan Province, Bagram offers a prime location to carry out surveillance operations in Central Asia, Iran, Pakistan, and western China. Local residents noted that for years, many residents assumed Washington would never abandon an asset of such strategic value. | | ---|---|--- Food vendors outside the Bagram Air Base, on Sept. 10, 2026. Photo by Emran Feroz for Drop Site News. War Memories For many living near the base, the departure of foreign forces marked the collapse of the local economy. "Business was good when the Americans were here," said Mohammad Musa, 18, who runs a shop with his family near the base gates. "There were so many people buying goods every day." Under the foreign military presence, a complex ecosystem of primary contractors, subcontractors, and service providers injected significant capital into the surrounding villages. While the political and human costs of the war were severe, the financial ecosystem provided livelihoods for thousands of local families. "We worked and we could feed our families," Abdul Latif said, speaking openly despite the presence of Taliban intelligence personnel nearby. "For us, that part was not bad." The accompanying officers listened to these statements without intervening or penalizing the speakers, though they occasionally countered with official regime rhetoric regarding national sovereignty and victory over foreign occupation. These interactions reflect a nuanced reality of the conflict: for those living in its immediate radius, the foreign presence was not experienced solely through the lens of military occupation, but also as a commercial opportunity. Five years into Taliban governance, remnants of that economic dependence linger in local memory. For others, Bagram remains defined by the systemic abuses that took place inside its prisons. Throughout the war, the base's detention center operated largely outside international legal oversight. Detainees were held for years without charge or legal representation. Notable instances of fatal abuse, including the 2002 deaths of Afghan detainees Dilawar and Habibullah at the hands of U.S. personnel, were documented in subsequent military investigations and investigative reports. Mufti Abdul Ahad Hakimi, now a high-ranking Taliban official, spent several years imprisoned at Bagram during the war. "I was tortured by both American soldiers and their Afghan counterparts," Hakimi said, describing prolonged physical and psychological pressure aimed at forcing him to switch political loyalties. "They wanted us to accept their system. I refused." Hakimi was eventually released as part of the large-scale prisoner exchanges conducted under the administration of President Ashraf Ghani following the February 2020 U.S.-Taliban agreement signed in Doha. Many of those who served prison terms there during the war and suffered torture at the hands of U.S. and Afghan government troops had no ties to militant groups. "The majority of the people detained in Bagram were not combatants," he said. "They were ordinary civilians swept up in raids because they lived in active zones or had loose ties to prominent figures." For Hakimi, the collapse of the Afghan republic in August 2021 marked a complete reversal: "When August 15 came, we returned to Bagram not as prisoners, but as its liberators." Who Is Inside Now? Bagram's legacy as a prison facility has generated a second set of rumors about its current role. Reports across Afghanistan suggest that the Taliban are utilizing the facility to hold criminal suspects, alleged members of Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP), and political dissidents. Hakimi acknowledged that parts of the facility remain operational under the Ministry of Defense, though he declined to specify the number of detainees, their identities, or the legal standards governing their detention. Outside the walls, daily routines around the Bagram bazaar continue uninterrupted between moments of tension. Convoys of Taliban vehicles occasionally pass through the outer gates, but the surrounding district remains quiet. For two decades, Bagram existed as a high-security enclave of foreign military power; today, those living beside it find themselves navigating both the legacy of that presence and the lingering threat of a new regional conflict. "It was completely different back then," said Mohammad Musa from his shop near the road. "Now, everything has gone quiet." Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. When we were outspent 16-to-1 in our primary, the political establishment said we didn't stand a chance. But we built a powerhouse grassroots movement, proved that people power can beat big money, and won. Now, they're saying Florida is too red to flip, but once again, they are wrong. A brand-new public poll was released, and it is sending shockwaves through Tallahassee and Washington: the U.S. Senate race is tied at 47-47. = = This isn't a surprise to me. Having organized across Florida for decades, I know firsthand that working families are fed up. Across our state, everyday Floridians are feeling the crush of skyrocketing insurance premiums, soaring rent, and corporate price-gouging on essentials. Meanwhile, our opponent, an unelected rubber stamp for billionaire donors, is deeply unpopular. A grand jury report has raised serious questions about whether she knew about a scheme that diverted public funds away from healthcare for impoverished children to pay for political advertisements. We are taking our message directly to every corner of Florida, engaging communities that have been ignored for far too long. But to keep this momentum going and compete against special interest money, we need the resources to launch our statewide field program and get our first round of TV ads on the air. This race is tied, and victory is within our reach, but only if we have the fuel to power our campaign across the finish line, with Election Day closing in fast. = = Whether it's $5, $10, or $25, every dollar makes a massive difference in a grassroots campaign like ours. Let's prove the doubters wrong once again. name: Cooper, Roy
subject: You’re outstanding, Peter
body:
I want to express my profound gratitude for having you by my side.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1598&source=&t=1&akid=4264%2E124072%2ETi68sJ) | | | | | | Peter, I’m not reaching out to everyone today – just a select few, including you.
---
| | My team was going through our supporter records, and yours stood out in the crowd. You’re one of my most attentive grassroots supporters. You’ve been getting these emails for a while now, and we see you're keeping up with the latest on this election. I want you to know that I know how engaged you’ve been with our campaign and how much I appreciate it. [**_Today, I’m asking you to take the next step._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1598&amount=5&t=9&akid=4264%2E124072%2ETi68sJ) **Here’s why:**
---
| | Grassroots fundraising has stalled recently, and it couldn’t come at a worse time. Republican super PACs have poured tens of millions into North Carolina to defeat me, and President Trump and JD Vance have both come to smear my name at rallies alongside my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley.
---
| | We need to turn this around fast – and the first step is getting our fundraising back on track. [**_Will you chip in $5 right now to help us reach today's goal? The stakes could not be higher._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1598&amount=5&t=10&akid=4264%2E124072%2ETi68sJ)

| | **Unlike my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley, I’m not a Washington DC insider who can rely on his billionaire connections to buy this Senate seat. I’m depending on people like you giving what you can, when you can, at crucial moments like this.**
---
| | _With 28 days left until the election, Peter, I need you._

subject: Climate change is here. But we’re not hopeless.
body:
Fuel the climate fight year-round| | |
---
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/140822483/651627892/779512579?sourceid=1168921&ms=DR_EM3&utm_campaign=K2D-1168921&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ2MTE1NGM1LWMyYzEtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zQGOW_ixxlcgLmdxloqwsbPdjlnqT9XJKsfw2IvRc8c=&emci=90fd53ea-d3c0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=d61154c5-c2c1-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=1504551)

| | |
---
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/140822485/651627894/-1516588317?sourceid=1168921&ms=DR_EM3&utm_campaign=K2D-1168921&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ2MTE1NGM1LWMyYzEtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zQGOW_ixxlcgLmdxloqwsbPdjlnqT9XJKsfw2IvRc8c=&emci=90fd53ea-d3c0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=d61154c5-c2c1-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=1504551)
---
---
Dear Peter,
---
As Director of Science for Save the Redwoods League, I spend a lot of time thinking about climate change. That means I also spend a lot of time asking myself hard questions: _What can we save? What _**_should_** _ we save? What might we be missing?_ Science can inform these questions, but if we are to truly combat climate change and protect what we love, we must lead with our values. We must listen to one another, strive to do better, commit to doing the right thing, and see it through. The challenges are great, but so is our resolve. **Our values at Save the Redwoods lead us to think not just about what we can**** _save_****, but what we can _grow._[What can you and I do, right now, to better the environment for future generations?](https://click.everyaction.com/k/140822487/651627896/-1516588317?sourceid=1168921&ms=DR_EM3&utm_campaign=K2D-1168921&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ2MTE1NGM1LWMyYzEtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zQGOW_ixxlcgLmdxloqwsbPdjlnqT9XJKsfw2IvRc8c=&emci=90fd53ea-d3c0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=d61154c5-c2c1-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=1504551)** The answer lies with the redwoods themselves.
---
---
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/140822489/651627898/-1516588317?sourceid=1168921&ms=DR_EM3&utm_campaign=K2D-1168921&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ2MTE1NGM1LWMyYzEtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zQGOW_ixxlcgLmdxloqwsbPdjlnqT9XJKsfw2IvRc8c=&emci=90fd53ea-d3c0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=d61154c5-c2c1-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=1504551)
---
---
Climate change is an undeniable danger to the redwoods. It amplifies every threat, from drought to invasive species. In the last decade alone, 17% of mature giant sequoias have been lost to extreme wildfires. But these trees are also our greatest allies in this fight. Coast redwoods store more carbon than any other forest ecosystem on Earth. **That is why I’m asking you to help us protect and restore the redwoods, helping to foster climate resilience, carbon storage, and awe-inspiring beauty for generations to come.** **[Right now, a generous Save the Redwoods Councilor, Peggy Light, has agreed to match all new Evergreen Memberships with a $250 contribution.
